Seven sections: which estimator is primary (paired per-episode wherever pairing exists; fold-level is a stability check, never primary unless shown powered in advance); what is forbidden at small n (a bootstrap over same-signed observations, and quoting a confidence level the estimator cannot respond to); what replaces it (t-interval, exact sign-flip permutation, noncentral-t MDE, all three reported together because they disagree usefully); MDE stated before every experiment with the known values tabulated; multiple testing over the honest family; controls; and what a guard must satisfy. THE PERMUTATION FLOOR IS NOW A PRE-RUN CHECK: one-sided p cannot go below 2^-n, so a design whose floor exceeds its corrected threshold CANNOT SUCCEED and is redesigned or declared underpowered before compute is spent. RULES.md gains R29-R33, all earned this session: a fix to a control changes the test; a resampling interval over same-signed observations is not a test; noticing a defect and continuing to rely on it is worse than missing it; an unresolvable question can be made irrelevant; 'the code does X' and 'the artifact contains X' are different claims.
experiments.implication: Romano-Wolf is named as the right tool and recorded as UNAVAILABLE with the reason -- it needs raw per-fold statistics for every family member and the ledger stores only summaries, so retrofitting means re-running the family. Bonferroni over the honest family size is the conservative fallback until that infrastructure exists. Recorded as missing rather than waved away.

experiments.question: Does NOCTUA's own headline claim -- that it beats Log-HAR -- survive the protocol just locked?
experiments.rule: Apply the locked protocol to the INCUMBENT, not only to candidates. A standard applied only to challengers is not a standard. Computed from the cached out-of-sample components, no retraining.
experiments.result:
THE SAME EPISTEMIC POSITION AS THE NEW CANDIDATE, which is the point of checking. Per-fold deltas -0.02216 / -0.01049 / +0.01563 / -0.02031 / -0.02317 / -0.03091, so 5 of 6 folds better and 2023 the exception. Relative improvement -4.98%.
FOLD LEVEL (n=6): deltas are NOT all same-signed, so a bootstrap here IS a legitimate test -- unlike E2c's, and that distinction matters. But the t-interval unadjusted is [-0.03253, +0.00206] and DOES NOT CLEAR; permutation one-sided p = 0.04688 against a floor of 0.01562; and observed |0.01524| is BELOW the noncentral-t MDE of 0.02348.
PAIRED PER-EPISODE (n=2,046): 1,157 episodes better and 889 worse, so the estimator can fail. Mean -0.014127, clearing at unadjusted [-0.020651, -0.006773], at family=9 [-0.023396, -0.003810], and at family=47 [-0.024995, -0.002314].
experiments.implication: The project's headline claim was NEVER fold-level significant either. It is established episode by episode and unresolved across years, exactly like E2c. That is the fair comparison and it changes how both should be described: the new candidate is not held to a bar the incumbent clears, because the incumbent does not clear it. This also puts the 4.98% figure in context. BENCHMARK's model table reports NOCTUA 0.290346 against log_har 0.305651 as a settled ranking. It is settled at the episode level; at the year level, with six folds, it is below the minimum detectable effect and one fold (2023) reverses it.
experiments.lesson: A standard applied only to challengers is not a standard, it is a moat. Running the protocol against the incumbent was the obvious next step and I nearly went off to build new benchmarks instead.

experiments.question: Before building the four-horizon volatility matrix: which rows can a 6-fold experiment resolve?
experiments.rule: STATS_PROTOCOL section 4 applied before the build. Noise floor from a model-free comparison -- persistence against a per-fold OLS Log-HAR fit -- so the MDE is a property of the design, not of any candidate. Reference effect size is NOCTUA's own measured advantage over Log-HAR, 4.98% (incumbent-under-protocol).
experiments.result: NOT ONE OF THE FOUR HORIZONS IS COMFORTABLY FOLD-LEVEL POWERED. MDE at 80% power, as a percentage of the persistence baseline: H=1 5.21%; H=6 11.76%; H=24 31.68%; H=168 65.48%. Against a 4.98% reference effect that is: 1h MARGINAL (MDE just exceeds it), 6h NOT POWERED by 2.4x, 1d NOT POWERED by 6.4x, 1w NOT POWERED by 13x. Underlying fold-level sd of the QLIKE difference: 0.02286 / 0.03730 / 0.10045 / 0.28115, rising steeply with horizon as the effective number of independent episodes falls.
experiments.implication:
THE MATRIX IS STILL WORTH BUILDING, but every row is scored PER-EPISODE as primary with the fold-level interval reported and labelled underpowered -- which is what STATS_PROTOCOL section 1 already prescribes. What this measurement prevents is spending the compute to produce fold-level numbers and only then discovering they cannot decide anything.
A SEPARATE STRUCTURAL FINDING, not about power: the sign of the Log-HAR-minus-persistence difference FLIPS with horizon. At H=1 Log-HAR is WORSE than plain persistence (+0.18831); at H=6 they are indistinguishable (-0.00251); at H=24 and H=168 Log-HAR wins decisively (-0.18126, -0.43014). That is mechanically sensible -- the HAR cascade's shortest component is DAILY, so it has nothing to say about a one-hour horizon -- and it means THE 1h ROW NEEDS A DIFFERENT BASELINE FAMILY. Quoting Log-HAR as the baseline to beat at 1h would be beating a model that is worse than doing nothing.
experiments.lesson: The power check keeps paying for itself. It has now pre-emptively caught three underpowered designs -- the blend weight, three of four direction horizons, and three of four volatility horizons -- and each time the alternative was to spend the compute first and learn it afterwards.

experiments.question: Across four horizons (1h, 6h, 1d, 1w), does NOCTUA beat the mandatory baseline family on QLIKE, and does the answer survive regime and worst-fold breakdowns?
experiments.rule:
PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE model/eval/vol_matrix.py exists. POPULATION: episodes_h4.parquet (H in {1,6,24,168}) joined to the per-anchor feature table, walk-forward folds, test slices only, all arms scored on IDENTICAL episodes. TARGET: QLIKE against realized RV over the forward window; the log hourly vol RATE is the regression target and sigma = exp(yhat)*sqrt(H) is what is scored, so every arm is compared on the same object. ARMS, all mandatory: persistence (exp(har_1d)*sqrt(H) -- NOT episodes.RV1, which looks forward and correlates 0.953 with the target); log_har (har_1d/5d/22d); har_short (har_1h/6h/1d/5d/22d) which is the baseline family the 1h row needs because vol-matrix-power found log_har is WORSE than persistence at H=1 (+0.18831); garch_normal and garch_t refit per fold on hourly returns and aggregated to exactly H hours; and NOCTUA trained ONE MULTI-HORIZON NETWORK PER FOLD on all four horizons jointly, with the horizon as an input feature and the shipped blend. [AMENDMENT, recorded 2026-08-28 while the smoke test was still running and BEFORE any number existed -- model/artifacts/vol_matrix.json did not yet exist and the H=1 smoke run had produced no output. The original text said 'trained per horizon per fold'. That would have been FOUR SEPARATE MODELS, none of which is NOCTUA: the shipped architecture is a single network conditioned on cal_H, trained on H in {6,12,19,24} jointly. A per-horizon network is a different model family wearing the same name, and scoring it would have answered a question nobody asked. The joint fit on {1,6,24,168} is the faithful analogue and also avoids the alternative error of scoring the SHIPPED artifact at H=1 and H=168, which are outside its trained horizon range -- extrapolation dressed up as a horizon study. Nothing else in this rule changes; the primary, the family size, the baseline ladder and the rejection condition are all as first written.] PRIMARY: paired PER-EPISODE moving-block bootstrap on the QLIKE difference between NOCTUA and the BEST BASELINE AT THAT HORIZON, chosen by pooled train/calib QLIKE and NEVER by test. The fold-level interval is reported beside it and LABELLED UNDERPOWERED at every horizon, because vol-matrix-power measured the fold-level MDE at 5.21%/11.76%/31.68%/65.48% of the persistence baseline against a 4.98% reference effect -- H=1 is marginal and the other three are not powered. MULTIPLE TESTING: this is a NEW family (volatility matrix). Family size fixed now at 4 horizons x 1 primary contrast = 4; Bonferroni within it. Failed rows stay in the family. BREAKDOWNS, reported for every row and NOT pass conditions: spike vs calm, per-year, WORST FOLD. REJECTION: if the paired CI contains zero against the best baseline at a horizon, NOCTUA has not been shown to beat the baseline family at that horizon and the row is recorded as such.

[SECOND AMENDMENT, 2026-08-28. THE BLOCK LENGTH. The original rule said 'paired PER-EPISODE moving-block bootstrap' and did not name a block length, so `mean_ci`'s default of round(n^(1/3)) would have governed. That default is a rule of thumb about SAMPLE SIZE and knows nothing about the dependence it exists to absorb. This table is anchored HOURLY with an H-hour forward window, so consecutive episodes share H-1 of their H hours and the dependence range is H regardless of n. At H=168 with n~49,000 the default gives 37 -- about a fifth of the overlap -- and the interval would be treating four fifths of a shared window as independent evidence. The primary interval now blocks at 2H, floored at the n^(1/3) value so it can never be SHORTER than the default, and the n^(1/3) interval is reported beside it for the two NOCTUA arms as a sensitivity, with any disagreement in verdict printed explicitly and the longer block governing.
WHAT HAD BEEN SEEN WHEN THIS WAS DECIDED, stated because it is the only thing that makes an amendment checkable: one row, from an H=24 single-seed smoke run -- noctua +0.00583 vs har_short, CI [-0.00488, +0.01455], DOES NOT CLEAR. Nothing at H=1, 6 or 168 had been computed; the full run was killed at fold 2023 and restarted. The amendment can only WIDEN every interval, so it can only make a row harder to pass -- it is not a route to a result, and the one row already seen was already a failure at the narrower setting.]
experiments.result:
TWO ROWS CLEAR, TWO DO NOT, AND THE TWO THAT CLEAR ARE QUALIFIED BY A CONFOUND FOUND AFTERWARDS (see implication). Pooled QLIKE over 6 folds, ~49,000 test episodes per horizon, baseline chosen on CALIB:
  H=1   best baseline har_short 0.5404. noctua 0.6718 (-0.13136), noctua40 0.6227 (-0.08231). BOTH DO NOT CLEAR -- and not marginally: the CI is [-0.16479, -0.08011], i.e. NOCTUA is 24% WORSE than har_short and worse than garch_t (0.5744) and garch_normal (0.6033) too.
  H=6   best baseline har_short 0.3833. noctua 0.4491 (-0.06579) CI [-0.08760, -0.04557], noctua40 0.4310 (-0.04770). BOTH DO NOT CLEAR; NOCTUA is 17% worse and again loses to both GARCHs.
  H=24  best baseline har_short 0.3156. noctua 0.2852 (+0.03032) CI [+0.01677, +0.04250] CLEARS, a 9.6% relative improvement. noctua40 0.3284 (-0.01289) DOES NOT CLEAR.
  H=168 best baseline log_har 0.3503. noctua NOT EVALUABLE (seas_1d and seas_5d do not exist at that horizon). noctua40 0.2057 (+0.14462) CI [+0.10042, +0.19624] CLEARS, a 41% relative improvement, and it is also better on the spike slice (1.0790 vs 1.7401) and on the worst fold (0.2779 vs 0.4504).
EVERY VERDICT IS UNCHANGED AT THE n^(1/3) BLOCK LENGTH, so none of them turns on the block-length amendment.
THE ABLATION THAT FELL OUT AT H=24, and it is the sharpest thing in the table: the two seasonal columns seas_1d and seas_5d carry the ENTIRE H=24 advantage. Dropping them turns +0.03032 (clears) into -0.01289 (does not). Both arms are scored on identical episodes at that horizon, so this is a feature effect and not a sample effect.
experiments.implication:
A CONFOUND I DID NOT SEE WHEN WRITING THE RULE, stated because it cuts against the two rows that clear. THE SCORED OLS BASELINES ARE HORIZON-BLIND AND NOCTUA IS NOT. `log_har` is fitted on har_1d/5d/22d and `har_short` adds har_1h/6h; neither has a horizon term. They are fitted ONCE per fold on the POOLED training sample spanning H in {1,6,24,168}, so each emits a single log hourly vol RATE whatever horizon it is asked about. NOCTUA takes cal_H as an input and can condition on the horizon. The target har_target = log(RV) - 0.5 log(H) is designed to be roughly horizon-invariant, which is why this is defensible enough to have escaped notice, but mean reversion means the average hourly rate over a WEEK is not the average hourly rate over an HOUR, and a pooled fit is a straw man at the extreme horizons. H=168 is the most extreme horizon in the table and it is where the margin is largest.
Worse, this repository ALREADY CONTAINS the fair version and I did not put it in the arm list: `log_har_cal` in noctua/baselines.py is har_1d/5d/22d PLUS cal_H and cal_weekend_frac, and its own comment describes it as 'a fairer well-specified bar'. It is used as NOCTUA's blend anchor and was never scored as a competitor.
WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT CHANGE. It does NOT rescue H=1 or H=6: NOCTUA loses there by 24% and 17% DESPITE holding the horizon-information advantage, which makes those two rejections stronger rather than weaker. It does NOT touch the H=24 ablation, since both NOCTUA arms face the same baseline. It DOES put the H=24 and H=168 margins in question, and the H=168 margin most of all.
So the verdict is ADVANCE, not ADOPT: the rule was applied verbatim and two rows cleared it, and the shipped model is unchanged. `vol-matrix-fair` is registered to resolve the confound with the baselines refitted PER HORIZON and `log_har_cal` added, and its result is reported whatever it says.
experiments.lesson: A baseline ladder is only as honest as its weakest rung, and the rung I got wrong was one the repository had already built and named for me. `log_har_cal` was sitting in baselines.py with a comment calling it the fairer bar, and I listed `log_har` and `har_short` in the pre-registration without asking whether they could see what the candidate could see. THE ASYMMETRY TO CHECK BEFORE REGISTERING A COMPARISON IS INFORMATIONAL, NOT ARCHITECTURAL: not 'is the baseline simpler' but 'is the baseline allowed to know the same things'.

experiments.question: What economic validation can this repository perform honestly, and what can it not?
experiments.rule: A scoping decision recorded BEFORE any economic number is produced, so that the boundary is not drawn afterwards around whatever happened to be computable.
experiments.result:
AN OPTIONS P&L CANNOT BE PRODUCED HONESTLY AND WILL NOT BE PRODUCED.
Checked, not assumed: `model/artifacts/datasources.json` records 18 probes, 2 reachable. Every crypto exchange API and every data aggregator returns 403 through the container's egress proxy. The only option-adjacent series in this repository is the Deribit DVOL volatility INDEX, in `iv_features.parquet` -- seven columns, all derived from an index level. There are no strikes, no expiries, no bid/ask, no size, no trade prints. `data/` holds spot OHLC for BTC, ETH, LTC, SOL, XRP and nothing else.
A volatility P&L therefore cannot be computed. It could only be SIMULATED -- by pricing hypothetical options off a model, assuming a spread, and assuming fills -- and every one of those assumptions would be doing more work than the forecast being tested. The protocol says do not manufacture one, and there is nothing here to manufacture it from.
experiments.implication:
WHAT REMAINS POSSIBLE, and is pre-registered separately as `econ-voltarget`: a VOLATILITY-TARGETING OVERLAY on spot BTC. Position size = target_vol / forecast_vol, rebalanced at each anchor. This uses only spot prices, which this repository has at 1-minute resolution, and a stated cost assumption. It is a RISK-CONTROL test, not a P&L claim: the question it answers is whether a better volatility forecast delivers a portfolio whose REALISED volatility sits closer to its target, and what the rebalancing costs. That is the actual commercial use of a volatility forecast for anyone without an options book, and it is measurable here without inventing a single price.
WHAT IS ALSO NOT POSSIBLE, and is worth saying because its absence is not obvious: a directional trading backtest has nothing to trade. `D1-direction-bench` returned NULL at all four horizons with n ~ 49,000 per horizon. Running a spot long/short strategy off a signal already shown to carry no information would produce a P&L chart that is a random walk with a fee drag, and presenting it would be theatre.
experiments.lesson: The honest scope of an economic test is set by the data on disk, not by the deliverable list. Writing down what cannot be done -- and why, with the artifact cited -- is a deliverable in itself.

experiments.question: Does a better volatility forecast produce a better-controlled portfolio once rebalancing costs are charged?
experiments.rule:
PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE the harness exists and BEFORE any number is seen.
DESIGN: a volatility-targeting overlay on spot BTC. At each anchor, weight w_t = clip(target / sigma_hat_t, 0, W_MAX). The portfolio return over the window is w_t * R_t. Every arm uses the SAME anchors, the SAME target and the SAME cap; the only thing that varies is which forecast supplies sigma_hat.
ARMS: the same ladder as `vol-matrix` -- persistence, log_har, har_short, garch_normal, garch_t, noctua, noctua40 -- plus a CONSTANT-WEIGHT arm (w = the train-window mean of the target/sigma ratio), which is the do-nothing control an overlay has to beat to justify its turnover.
PRIMARY: |realised annualised volatility - target|, pooled over test folds, with a paired moving-block bootstrap CI on the per-fold absolute deviation. Lower is better. This is a RISK-CONTROL endpoint and is stated as the primary precisely because it is the one a volatility forecast is entitled to be judged on.
SECONDARY, reported and NOT pass conditions: turnover (mean |w_t - w_{t-1}|), cost-adjusted return, realised Sharpe, and the maximum drawdown. Return-based quantities are secondary because BTC's spot drift dominates them and no volatility forecast controls it -- a arm can win on Sharpe purely by having been more levered during a bull fold.
COSTS: charged, stated, and varied. Base case 10 bps round-trip on traded notional (5 bps taker fee + 5 bps slippage), with 5 and 25 bps reported as a sensitivity. These are ASSUMPTIONS, not measurements: this repository has no order book and no fee schedule, so the number is a stated premise and the sensitivity is how its influence is bounded. If the ranking of arms changes across the three cost levels, the result is reported as COST-DEPENDENT and no arm is declared better.
TARGET: 60% annualised, chosen because it is close to BTC's own long-run realised level so the overlay is neither systematically de-levering nor levering; W_MAX = 3.0.
REJECTION: if the paired CI on |realised - target| contains zero against the best baseline, the better forecast has NOT been shown to produce a better-controlled portfolio, and that is the result.
experiments.result: pre-registered, not yet run
experiments.implication: EXPECTED OUTCOME, recorded so it cannot be fitted afterwards. QLIKE differences between these arms are of order 0.01-0.03 on a base of 0.28. Realised-volatility control is a much blunter instrument than QLIKE: it depends on the forecast only through the RATIO target/sigma_hat, and a forecast that is biased by a constant factor is perfectly re-scalable and loses nothing. I therefore expect the arms to be MUCH closer on this endpoint than on QLIKE, and I expect the constant-weight control to be competitive. A NULL is the likely outcome and would be the honest one. What would genuinely surprise me is an arm beating the constant-weight control after costs at all three cost levels.

experiments.question: Do the two rows that cleared vol-matrix survive a baseline family that is allowed to know the horizon?
experiments.rule:
PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE the fair-baseline code exists and BEFORE any number from it has been seen. This supersedes nothing: `vol-matrix`'s verdicts stand as recorded, applied verbatim to the rule as written. This entry resolves a CONFOUND that entry names against itself.
THE CHANGE, and it is the only change: every OLS baseline is refitted SEPARATELY PER HORIZON on that fold's training episodes at that horizon, instead of once on the pooled sample spanning all four; and `log_har_cal` (har_1d/5d/22d + cal_H + cal_weekend_frac) joins the arm list. Together these give the baseline family the same horizon information NOCTUA has. Everything else is held fixed: same episodes, same folds, same target, same QLIKE, same seeds, same 2H block length, same best-baseline-chosen-on-calib rule, same primary, same Bonferroni denominator of 4.
PRIMARY, unchanged in form: paired per-episode moving-block CI on NOCTUA minus the best baseline at that horizon, chosen on calib. REJECTION: if a row that cleared in `vol-matrix` no longer clears here, THE FAIR VERSION GOVERNS and the row is recorded as not established. A margin that exists only against a baseline denied the candidate's inputs is not a margin.
experiments.result: pre-registered, not yet run
experiments.implication:
EXPECTED OUTCOME, recorded so it cannot be fitted afterwards.
H=1 and H=6: I expect NOCTUA to still lose, and by more. It already loses by 24% and 17% while HOLDING the horizon advantage, so removing that advantage should widen the gap. If either row flips to a NOCTUA win under a STRONGER baseline, something is wrong with the harness and I will look for the bug before reporting the win.
H=24: I expect the +0.03032 margin to SHRINK and I genuinely do not know whether it survives. H=24 is close to the pooled centre of the four horizons, so the horizon-blind fit is least penalised there, which argues the margin is mostly real; but har_short at H=24 also benefits least from a per-horizon refit for the same reason.
H=168: I expect the +0.14462 margin to shrink SUBSTANTIALLY, and this is the row I am most prepared to lose. It is the most extreme horizon, so the pooled fit is most mis-specified there, and a 41% relative improvement at a one-week horizon is larger than anything else this project has measured. Extraordinary margins in the row where the baseline is weakest are the ordinary signature of a weak baseline.
A result where ALL FOUR rows fail is a legitimate and publishable outcome and would mean the volatility matrix's honest summary is that NOCTUA does not beat a properly specified HAR family at any horizon.

experiments.question: Does any direction model beat the rolling base rate as a PROBABILITY forecast, once the features are built at each episode's own horizon?
experiments.rule: IDENTICAL to `D1-direction-bench`. Not one character of the rule changed -- the same primary (paired per-episode Brier Skill Score against the CALIB-WINDOW base rate), the same guards (calibration slope in [0.8,1.2], intercept within 0.02 of zero, must beat a row-shuffled label control and a circular-time-shift placebo), the same family size of 16, the same AUC-is-reported-not-a-condition. ONLY THE INPUTS CHANGED: features are now built by `noctua.features.build_features` on the h4 episodes, so `cal_weekend_frac`, `seas_1d`, `seas_5d` and `seas_22d` are computed at each episode's own horizon instead of being joined per anchor from the H=6 row. See BENCHMARK.md section 30.
experiments.result:
THE NULL IS UNCHANGED, AND THE ARMS GOT SLIGHTLY BETTER. 8 of 8 model arms fail. Brier / BSS-vs-calib / AUC / calibration slope:
  H=1   (n=49,123) logistic 0.25093 -0.00342 auc 0.5090 slope 0.052 | gbm 0.25046 -0.00154 auc 0.5148 slope 0.052
  H=6   (n=49,124) logistic 0.25286 -0.00972 auc 0.5046 slope 0.012 | gbm 0.25119 -0.00306 auc 0.5128 slope 0.038
  H=24  (n=49,106) logistic 0.25906 -0.02726 auc 0.4993 slope 0.004 | gbm 0.25608 -0.01546 auc 0.5116 slope -0.000
  H=168 (n=48,962) logistic 0.26282 -0.02053 auc 0.5216 slope 0.021 | gbm 0.28142 -0.09271 auc 0.5015 slope -0.027
The paired per-episode CI excludes zero on the ADVERSE side (arm worse than the calib base rate) in 5 of 8 model rows and straddles zero in 3. No arm clears. Both negative controls are negative at all four horizons -- shuffled -0.00231 / -0.00678 / -0.01448 / -0.00523, placebo -0.01384 / -0.00737 / -0.02032 / -0.03762 -- so the harness is not manufacturing skill.
WHAT THE CORRECTION MOVED, since that is the reason it was run: at H=1 the arms improved (gbm BSS -0.00361 -> -0.00154, AUC 0.5123 -> 0.5148) and gbm's paired CI went from excluding zero adversely to straddling it. So the mis-specified features WERE hurting the arms, exactly as suspected -- and correcting them was still not nearly enough. Every calibration slope remains between -0.03 and +0.06 against a required [0.8, 1.2].
experiments.implication:
DIRECTION IS CLOSED as a probability-forecasting problem at 1h, 6h, 1d and 1w with this feature set and these two model classes, and the closure now rests on correct inputs. It is not a power failure: n is about 49,000 per horizon and the intervals are narrow enough to exclude zero in the adverse direction in most rows.
THE CALIBRATION SLOPE IS THE RESULT, not the Brier score. A model with no signal does not emit a flat forecast -- it emits a confident, varying one whose variation is noise. The Brier score barely notices (0.2505 against 0.2501 at H=1); the calibration slope reports it as 0.05 against a required 1.0. Pre-registering calibration as a PASS condition and AUC as REPORTED-ONLY is the only reason this is not being written up as 'AUC 0.515, a small but consistent edge'.
TWO OBSERVATIONS THAT SURVIVE THE NULL AND CHANGE NOTHING. (1) gbm's AUC is above 0.5 at all four horizons (0.5148 / 0.5128 / 0.5116 / 0.5015). If rank information exists it is at that scale, and it is more than destroyed by the miscalibration. (2) At H=168 the TRAIN base rate beats the CALIB base rate with a CI excluding zero, [-0.013279, -0.000996]. That is a finding about BASE-RATE INSTABILITY -- the calibration window 2023-01 to 2024-07 had an unrepresentative drift -- and it vindicates pre-registering the calib-window base rate as the bar rather than the train one.
experiments.lesson: RERUNNING A NULL AGAINST FIXED INPUTS IS CHEAP AND THE ASTERISK IS FOREVER. This cost about twenty minutes and converted 'direction is closed, though the features were mis-specified' into 'direction is closed'. It also produced a measurement that could not have been guessed: the defect was worth roughly 0.002 BSS and one CI's worth of sign at H=1, i.e. real but far smaller than the gap to the baseline.

experiments.question: Do the two rows that cleared vol-matrix survive a baseline family that is allowed to know the horizon?
experiments.rule: As pre-registered in `vol-matrix-fair`. Not one character changed after the fact.
experiments.result:
NEITHER SURVIVES. ALL FOUR ROWS NOW FAIL. NOCTUA does not beat a properly specified HAR family at ANY of the four horizons, and the two margins that cleared under the horizon-blind baselines were the horizon-blindness.
  H=1   best baseline persistence (chosen on calib). noctua 0.6718 (-0.04578) FAILS. noctua40 0.6227 (+0.00328) CI [-0.01593, +0.02032] straddles zero -- statistically indistinguishable from doing nothing. THE BEST FORECASTER IN THE WHOLE TABLE AT THIS HORIZON IS garch_t: +0.05161 over persistence, CI [+0.03425, +0.07075], clearing favourably. A three-parameter conditional-variance model beats the 6,939-parameter network by 8% at one hour.
  H=6   best baseline har_short 0.41710. noctua 0.44907 (-0.03197) CI [-0.05017, -0.01162] FAILS. noctua40 (-0.01387) straddles.
  H=24  best baseline har_short 0.27818. noctua 0.28523 (-0.00705) CI [-0.02288, +0.00472]. THE +0.03032 WIN BECAME A -0.00705 LOSS. It no longer clears, and it is no longer even ahead.
  H=168 best baseline har_short 0.18207. noctua40 0.20569 (-0.02362) CI [-0.04914, -0.00588], which excludes zero on the ADVERSE side. THE +0.14462 '41% IMPROVEMENT' BECAME A -0.02362 LOSS THAT IS SIGNIFICANTLY WORSE THAN THE BASELINE.
Every verdict is unchanged at the n^(1/3) block length.
THE SIZE OF THE CONFOUND, measured rather than argued, by scoring both fits of the same family on the same episodes (pooled QLIKE / per-horizon QLIKE):
  H=1    har_short 0.52x   log_har 0.77x     (pooled was BETTER -- see below)
  H=6    har_short 0.92x   log_har 0.92x
  H=24   har_short 1.13x   log_har 1.12x
  H=168  har_short 2.06x   log_har 1.90x
At the one-week horizon the pooled fit was TWICE the loss of the per-horizon fit. The '41% NOCTUA improvement' was measured against a baseline that was itself 106% worse than the same model family fitted properly.
TWO THINGS THE CALIB-BASED SELECTION CAUGHT, and they are the reason it is in the rule. (1) At H=1 the per-horizon har_short EXPLODES -- QLIKE 1.03094, worst fold 2.83480, spike 12.4521 -- because five HAR regressors fitted on H=1 episodes alone overfit badly. Its calib QLIKE was 1.4016, the worst of the four candidates, so it was not selected; persistence was. A test-side selection would have handed NOCTUA a free win there. (2) At H=168 log_har and log_har_cal are IDENTICAL to five decimals, which is correct and is a self-check: cal_weekend_frac is exactly 2/7 for every 168-hour window and cal_H is constant within a horizon, so the two specifications coincide by construction at that horizon.
experiments.implication:
THE HONEST SUMMARY OF THE VOLATILITY MATRIX IS THAT NOCTUA DOES NOT BEAT A PROPERLY SPECIFIED HAR FAMILY AT ANY HORIZON TESTED, and at one hour it loses to GARCH(1,1) with Student-t innovations. The `vol-matrix` ADVANCE is withdrawn. The shipped model is unchanged, as it has been throughout.
THIS PUTS THE PROJECT'S OWN HEADLINE UNDER THE SAME QUESTION, and that has to be said plainly rather than left for someone else to notice. `eval/benchmark.py` scores `log_har` as the baseline for the production claim of a 4.98% NOCTUA advantage, and it fits that baseline ONCE on the pooled training sample spanning H in {6,12,19,24} -- the same horizon-blind fit, on a narrower horizon range. A 4x range is far less exposed than the 168x range here, and the H=6 column above (0.92x) suggests the effect is small in that regime rather than absent. But 'suggests' is not a measurement, and `E-prod-fairbaseline` is registered to measure it.
WHAT SURVIVES UNTOUCHED: the H=24 ablation from `vol-matrix`. seas_1d and seas_5d still carry a large part of NOCTUA's H=24 performance (noctua 0.28523 against noctua40 0.32844 on identical episodes), because both arms face the same baseline whichever baseline that is. That is a fact about the feature set and it is not affected by this correction.
experiments.lesson:
I PRE-REGISTERED THE EXPECTATION THAT I WOULD LOSE H=168 AND THEN LOST IT, WHICH IS THE ONLY REASON THIS READS AS A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN AS A RETRACTION. The recorded expectation said 'extraordinary margins in the row where the baseline is weakest are the ordinary signature of a weak baseline'; the row where the baseline was weakest turned out to be weak by a factor of two.
THE GENERALISABLE RULE, now R39: check whether the baseline is allowed to know what the candidate knows. Not 'is the baseline simpler' -- simpler is the point of a baseline -- but 'is it denied an input the candidate has'. NOCTUA sees cal_H; log_har and har_short did not. Every margin in the first matrix was partly a measurement of that asymmetry, and the largest margin was almost entirely it.
experiments.correction_note:
CORRECTION, 2026-08-28, to a claim in this entry's own `implication`, recorded here rather than edited away. I wrote that `eval/benchmark.py` 'scores log_har as the baseline for the production claim ... the same horizon-blind fit'. THAT IS WRONG. `benchmark.run_fold` builds its comparison from `bl["log_har_cal"]` -- har_1d/5d/22d PLUS cal_H and cal_weekend_frac -- and merely STORES the result under the dict key `"log_har"`. The incumbent baseline ALREADY HAS A HORIZON TERM, so the headline is not the straw-man comparison I assumed by analogy with the matrix.
I was misled by an artifact key that does not name what it holds, and I did not read the line that produces it before asserting what it was. The narrower question that remains -- does fitting that horizon-aware baseline POOLED across {6,12,19,24} rather than at H=19 cost it anything -- is real, and is what `E-prod-fairbaseline` measures. Everything else in this entry stands: the matrix's own scored baselines WERE horizon-blind, and that is measured, not assumed.

experiments.question: Does NOCTUA's headline production advantage over Log-HAR survive a horizon-aware baseline?
experiments.rule:
PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE the code exists and BEFORE any number from it has been seen. `vol-matrix-fair-result` showed that a Log-HAR fitted once on a pooled multi-horizon sample is a straw man at horizons far from the pooled centre, by a factor of two at the extreme. `eval/benchmark.py` fits its `log_har` baseline the same way -- once per fold on the pooled training sample spanning H in {6,12,19,24} -- and that baseline is what the project's headline 'NOCTUA beats Log-HAR by 4.98%' is measured against.
THE TEST: rescore the PRODUCTION slice (H=19, anchor 17:00 UTC, episodes.parquet, the same six walk-forward folds) with the baseline refitted PER HORIZON on H=19 training episodes, and with `log_har_cal` (which already carries cal_H and cal_weekend_frac) added as an arm. Everything else held fixed: same episodes, same seeds, same QLIKE, same paired per-episode primary with the 2H block length.
PRIMARY: paired per-episode CI on NOCTUA minus the best baseline at H=19, chosen on CALIB. FAMILY: this is one contrast; it joins the volatility-matrix family, taking it from 4 to 5, and the Bonferroni denominator is 5.
REJECTION: if the CI no longer excludes zero favourably, the 4.98% headline is not established against a horizon-aware baseline and BENCHMARK.md must say so wherever that number appears.

[CORRECTION TO THIS RULE'S PREMISE, 2026-08-28, made after the first run and BEFORE its result was accepted. The rule above says the headline is measured against a pooled `log_har`. It is measured against a pooled `log_har_cal`, which carries cal_H and cal_weekend_frac -- `benchmark.run_fold` stores the log_har_cal comparison under the key `log_har`. The first run therefore restated the incumbent claim against the WRONG ARM and is discarded, not reported. The arm list gains `log_har_cal_pooled` and the run is repeated. Nothing about the PRIMARY changes: it was always NOCTUA against the best CALIB-chosen horizon-aware baseline, and that contrast is unaffected by which arm the incumbent comparison is restated against.]
experiments.result: pre-registered, not yet run
experiments.implication:
EXPECTED OUTCOME, recorded so it cannot be fitted afterwards. I expect the headline to SHRINK but to SURVIVE, and I expect the shrinkage to be modest. The reasoning is the measured confound size as a function of horizon spread: the h4 table spans a 168x range and the pooled fit cost the baseline a factor of 2.06 at the extreme; episodes.parquet spans only 6 to 24, a 4x range, and the closest analogue in that range (H=6, the shortest horizon in a narrow set) showed the pooled fit was 0.92x -- i.e. pooling HELPED slightly there rather than hurting. H=19 sits near the middle of {6,12,19,24}, which is where a pooled fit is least mis-specified.
So my prediction is: the margin drops from 4.98% to somewhere in 2-5%, and still clears. IF IT DOES NOT CLEAR, the correct response is to say the headline is not established and to correct every place BENCHMARK.md states it -- not to look for a third baseline specification. Writing that down now is the point of writing it down now.

experiments.question: Does NOCTUA's headline production advantage over Log-HAR survive a horizon-aware baseline?
experiments.rule: As pre-registered, with the premise correction recorded in `E-prod-fairbaseline`.
experiments.result:
THE HEADLINE SURVIVES ITS OWN COMPARISON AND FAILS A BETTER ONE, AND THOSE ARE TWO DIFFERENT FINDINGS. Production slice, H=19 at 17:00 UTC, 2,046 test episodes over 6 folds, baseline chosen on CALIB, Bonferroni at family size 5 so intervals are 99%.
  THE INCUMBENT CLAIM IS CONFIRMED. NOCTUA vs `log_har_cal_pooled` -- the arm the published headline is actually measured against -- is +0.01420 (+4.56%), CI [+0.00300, +0.02339], which CLEARS. BENCHMARK.md's -6.14% is not overturned; run-to-run training variance and mean-of-folds versus pooled-over-episodes aggregation account for the gap between 4.56% and 6.14%.
  THE POOLING PENALTY IS SMALL HERE, exactly as predicted from the narrow horizon range. log_har_cal pooled across {6,12,19,24} scores 0.31122; refitted at H=19 it scores 0.30442. A 2.2% penalty, against the 106% penalty the same mechanism carried at H=168 in the matrix. The 4x range really is far less exposed than the 168x range.
  THE PRIMARY FAILS ANYWAY, FOR A DIFFERENT REASON. The best baseline by calib QLIKE is not log_har_cal at all -- it is `har_short` (calib 0.3163 against log_har_cal's 0.3251). On test, NOCTUA 0.29702 against har_short 0.30654 is +0.00951 (+3.10%), CI [-0.00897, +0.02448], which DOES NOT CLEAR. This is not a Bonferroni artifact: the unadjusted 95% interval [-0.00436, +0.02114] also straddles zero.
  NOCTUA still has the best pooled QLIKE of any arm in the table (0.29702). It is simply not SIGNIFICANTLY better than har_short at n=2,046 -- which is the production slice's whole sample, 365 episodes a fold.
experiments.implication:
THE HEADLINE'S PROBLEM IS NOT HORIZON-BLINDNESS. IT IS AN INCOMPLETE BASELINE FAMILY. `har_short` -- Corsi's cascade extended downward with har_1h and har_6h -- has been sitting in `noctua/baselines.py` the entire time and has never been scored as a competitor in `eval/benchmark.py`. It beats log_har_cal on calib and on test, and against it NOCTUA's advantage is +3.10% and not statistically established.
That is the second time in this session that the strongest available baseline turned out to already exist in this repository and to have been left out of the arm list -- log_har_cal in the matrix, har_short here. The pattern is not bad luck. `VOL_BASELINES` has six entries and `eval/benchmark.py` scores one of them.
WHAT MUST CHANGE IN THE DOCUMENTATION, per the pre-registered rejection: every statement of the form 'NOCTUA beats Log-HAR by X%' must say WHICH Log-HAR, and must be accompanied by the har_short comparison, because a reader entitled to the best available baseline is not getting it otherwise. The -6.14% figure itself is not withdrawn -- it is correct for the comparison it names.
WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: the shipped model. As throughout.
experiments.lesson:
MY PREDICTION WAS HALF RIGHT AND THE HALF I GOT WRONG IS THE INFORMATIVE HALF. I predicted the margin would land in 2-5% and still clear. It landed at 3.10% and did not clear. The magnitude reasoning -- confound size scales with horizon spread, 4x is much less exposed than 168x -- was sound and was confirmed at 2.2%. What I did not anticipate was that fixing the FIT would matter less than fixing the ROSTER: the per-horizon refit moved log_har_cal by 2.2%, while adding an arm that was already in the codebase moved the baseline by enough to erase significance.
GENERALISED: when auditing a comparison, enumerate the baseline family the repository ALREADY CONTAINS before asking whether the chosen baseline was fitted correctly. A missing arm is a larger error than a mis-fitted one and is cheaper to find.

experiments.question: Does a better volatility forecast produce a better-controlled portfolio once rebalancing costs are charged?
experiments.rule: As pre-registered in `econ-voltarget`. Not one character changed after the fact.
experiments.result:
NOCTUA FAILS THE PRE-REGISTERED PRIMARY, AND har_short WINS FOR A THIRD TIME. H=24, rebalanced at 00:00 UTC so windows do not overlap, 60% annualised target, weight capped at 3.0, 6 folds.
PRIMARY |realised annualised vol - 60%|, lower better: har_short 0.0577 (best, chosen on calib) | garch_t 0.0710 | noctua40 0.0808 | log_har 0.0822 | noctua 0.0823 | constant_w 0.0933 | garch_normal 0.0963 | persistence 0.1124. NOCTUA DOES NOT CLEAR.
AND THE ADVERSE DIRECTION IS NOT ESTABLISHED EITHER, which matters and is why the small-n instruments are in the protocol. The moving-block CI [-0.0531, -0.0049] excludes zero adversely; the t-interval [-0.0555, +0.0063] does NOT; and the observed |effect| of 0.0246 is BELOW the design's own 80%-power MDE of 0.0419. At n=6 folds the t-interval is the defensible instrument (STATS_PROTOCOL 2-3), so the honest statement is: NOCTUA fails to clear, and it is not shown to be worse either. Both noctua arms and the constant-weight control are NOT POWERED on this endpoint.
THE EXACT SIGN-FLIP PERMUTATION FLOOR BINDS: at n=6 the one-sided p cannot go below 2^-6 = 0.0156, and log_har and persistence both sit exactly AT that floor. No Bonferroni-corrected claim is available from this design at any effect size.
THE CONSTANT-WEIGHT CONTROL WINS ON RETURN AT EVERY COST LEVEL and does so with 58x LESS TURNOVER -- 0.0035 against NOCTUA's 0.2038. Net return at 5/10/25 bps: constant_w +0.140/+0.139/+0.137 against NOCTUA's +0.087/+0.053/-0.049. Sharpe at 10 bps: +0.209 against -0.047. NOCTUA's overlay goes NEGATIVE on net return by 25 bps; the constant weight barely moves, because it does not trade.
THE RANKING IS COST-DEPENDENT (identical at all three levels: False), so per the pre-registered rule NO ARM IS DECLARED BETTER ON RETURN. Reported honestly: the WINNER is stable -- constant_w is first at 5, 10 and 25 bps -- and only the lower positions permute. That observation does not change the declaration.
experiments.implication:
THE OVERLAY DOES NOT PAY FOR ITS OWN TURNOVER. Every forecast-driven arm trades 50-100x more than the constant weight and none of them beats it on net return at any cost level, while the best of them beats it on risk control by 0.0356 -- an effect below the MDE. That is the finding, and it is a NULL rather than a negative: this design cannot resolve the risk-control difference, and the return difference favours doing nothing.
A SEPARATE AND UNPREDICTED FINDING THAT SUPPORTS AN ALREADY-OPEN QUESTION. Every HAR-family and NOCTUA arm OVERSHOOTS the 60% target -- realised 0.6577 to 0.7124 -- while both GARCH arms UNDERSHOOT (0.5065, 0.5523). Overshooting means the sigma forecast was systematically too LOW, so the overlay levered up too far. That is exactly the signature `E-scale` predicts and has been sitting open on: the shipped model reports a conditional MEDIAN while QLIKE is minimised by the conditional MEAN of variance, and for a lognormal-ish distribution the median sits below the mean. This overlay measures the consequence in a unit anyone can read -- 8 percentage points of annualised volatility above a 60% target -- and it does so on an endpoint E-scale was never designed against. It is the strongest argument yet for closing E-scale, and it is NOT a licence to close it here: that experiment has its own pre-registered rule requiring both slices.
har_short WINNING A THIRD TIME, on a third endpoint, is now the most robust empirical fact in this phase. It beat every arm on QLIKE at H=6, 24 and 168 in the fair matrix, it beat log_har_cal on the production slice, and it beats everything on risk control here. It has been in noctua/baselines.py the whole time.
experiments.lesson:
MY PRE-REGISTERED EXPECTATION WAS RIGHT AND THAT IS WORTH AS LITTLE AS USUAL. I wrote that the arms would be much closer on this endpoint than on QLIKE, that the constant-weight control would be competitive, and that a NULL was the likely and honest outcome. All three held. The value was not in being right -- it was that writing it down beforehand made the constant-weight control a MANDATORY arm rather than an optional one, and the constant weight is what wins.
THE BOOTSTRAP AND THE t-INTERVAL DISAGREED, AND THE PROTOCOL HAD ALREADY DECIDED WHICH GOVERNS. Without STATS_PROTOCOL 2-3 written down in advance, an author with a bootstrap interval excluding zero and a t-interval straddling it gets to choose, and will choose the one that reads better.

experiments.question: Can NOCTUA learn only the residual of a cross-fitted teacher, and does that beat the teacher itself?
experiments.rule:
PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE the harness exists and before any Arm A number has been produced. Governed by research/TEACHER_ZOO.md, frozen earlier today.
ARCHITECTURE. All arithmetic in the log hourly vol RATE domain, which is the domain har_target already defines: y = log(RV) - 0.5*log(H), and a teacher's sigma maps to yhat_T = log(sigma_T) - 0.5*log(H). The residual target is r = y - yhat_T. NOCTUA is trained on r ALONE. The final forecast is yhat = yhat_T + rhat, scored as sigma = exp(yhat)*sqrt(H).
THE FAIL-SAFE IDENTITY, WHICH IS A PASS CONDITION AND NOT A REMARK: a residual model that predicts exactly zero must reproduce the teacher's QLIKE BIT-IDENTICALLY. This is asserted in code to 1e-12 before any arm is scored. It is what makes the architecture fail safely back to the stronger teacher, and if it does not hold then the composition is wrong and no Arm A number means anything.
TEACHER VALUES ARE CROSS-FITTED, ALWAYS. yhat_T comes from model/artifacts/teacher_oof.npz. The residual model trains on CALIB-slice teacher values and is scored on TEST-slice teacher values; train-slice teacher values do not exist. TEACHER_ZOO section 2.
THREE TREATMENT VARIANTS, all declared now:
  A1  har_short-residual. The teacher is har_short at every horizon, as specified. NOTE THIS IS       EXPECTED TO BE THE WRONG TEACHER AT H=1, where har_short scores 1.03094 -- worse than       doing nothing. A1 is run anyway and at that horizon it is a test of the RESIDUAL       MECHANISM's ability to rescue a bad teacher, not a test of har_short.
  A2  calib-selected-teacher-residual. The teacher is whichever teacher has the best CALIBRATION       QLIKE at that horizon, never test. This is the variant TEACHER_ZOO section 5's       no-universal-winner rule actually implies.
  A3  teacher-as-feature. The OOF teacher forecast enters as an ordinary input column and NOCTUA       predicts y directly. This separates 'the teacher's forecast is useful information' from       'the residual decomposition is the right inductive bias' -- if A3 matches A1/A2 then the       decomposition bought nothing and only the information mattered.
CONTROL, MANDATORY: A0, NOCTUA trained from scratch on y on the identical folds and episodes. Already measured in vol-matrix-fair; re-run inside this harness so the comparison is paired rather than cross-run.
PRIMARY: paired PER-EPISODE moving-block bootstrap, block max(n^(1/3), 2H), on the QLIKE difference between each arm and ITS OWN TEACHER at that horizon. Beating NOCTUA V1 is NOT the bar and is not reported as a pass. TEACHER_ZOO section 9.
FAMILY SIZE, FIXED NOW: 3 variants x 4 horizons = 12. Bonferroni within it. Failed cells stay in the family. A0 is a control and does not consume family budget.
NEGATIVE CONTROLS, both required per TEACHER_ZOO section 6: (i) SHUFFLED TEACHER -- teacher values permuted across episodes within the slice, destroying alignment while preserving the marginal distribution; (ii) ROTATED TEACHER -- teacher values circularly shifted in time. Neither may beat its unshuffled counterpart. If either does, the harness is broken and no verdict is issued.
POWER: the per-episode MDE is computed from teacher_oof.npz BEFORE the arm runs, per R5, and any horizon whose MDE exceeds the observed teacher-to-teacher spread is labelled NOT POWERED before the fact.
REJECTION: if an arm's paired CI against its own teacher contains zero, the residual decomposition has not been shown to improve on that teacher at that horizon, and the cell is recorded as such. If NO cell clears, Arm A is rejected and the mechanism tag `teacher-residual` takes its first strike under the stagnation rule.

[IMPLEMENTATION NOTE, recorded 2026-08-29 BEFORE any Arm A number exists. The rule says NOCTUA learns r = y - yhat_T and did not say how the teacher value on the TRAINING slice is obtained -- and TEACHER_ZOO section 2 forbids emitting train-slice teacher predictions at all, which would make the arm unconstructible. TEACHER_ZOO Amendment 1 resolves it: the train slice is split into an EXPANDING-FORWARD inner sequence, the teacher is fitted on inner blocks 1..k and predicts block k+1, and those inner out-of-fold values -- never in-sample ones -- form the residual target. Not K-fold: K-fold fits each held-out block partly on LATER blocks, which is look-ahead on a time series, and this repository already discarded one estimator for exactly that. The first inner block gets no teacher prediction and its episodes are DROPPED rather than given a fallback, because a fallback would be R43 -- inventing a number the model reads as information. Nothing about the primary, the family size or the rejection condition changes.]
experiments.result: pre-registered, not yet run
experiments.implication:
EXPECTED OUTCOME, recorded so it cannot be fitted afterwards.
The single most important piece of prior evidence is `E-anchor-verdict`: inserting har_1h and har_6h into NOCTUA's Log-HAR ANCHOR was HARMFUL -- spike QLIKE +1.87%, worse in 6 of 6 folds, CI excluding zero unfavourably -- and its stated mechanism was that the full pipeline ALREADY FEEDS har_1h and har_6h to the neural stage, so the treatment added no information and merely moved the noisiest RV window into the term whose job is stability.
That creates a genuine puzzle which Arm A is partly a probe of: NOCTUA already SEES the five har_short columns, and an OLS on exactly those five columns still beats it at H=6, 24 and 168. So the advantage cannot be the information. It must be the FUNCTIONAL FORM or the ESTIMATION -- a low-variance linear combination beating a flexible model that has the same inputs is the classic signature of variance, not bias.
If that reading is right, THE RESIDUAL DECOMPOSITION SHOULD HELP, because it hands the stable linear part to the estimator that does it well and asks the network only for the deviation. And A3 (teacher-as-feature) should help LESS than A1/A2, because a feature column can be ignored or diluted by the network while an additive offset cannot.
If instead A3 matches A1/A2, the decomposition bought nothing.
If ALL of A1, A2, A3 fail to beat their teachers, the honest reading is that NOCTUA's capacity is not the binding constraint and the project should stop trying to add capacity to it -- which would be a genuinely valuable negative result and is a real possible outcome.
MY POINT PREDICTION: A2 clears at H=24 and H=168, does not clear at H=6, and at H=1 the residual mechanism fails to rescue har_short in A1 while A2 (whose teacher there will be persistence or garch_t) does better than NOCTUA from scratch. I expect the margins to be SMALL -- a few percent -- because the teacher is already good and the residual is mostly noise.

experiments.question: A missing hour is encoded as 'volatility was 1e-6'. What does that cost, and what should Phase 2 do about it?
experiments.rule:
PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE the corrected treatment is run.
THE DEFECT, verified independently and not taken from an agent: `noctua/features.py` computes the HAR cascade as 0.5*_safe_log(max(rv, EPS)) with EPS=1e-12. An hour with NO TRADES -- volume exactly 0, rv5 exactly 0 -- therefore becomes har_1h = -13.8155, which is not 'missing' but the confident claim that realized volatility was 1e-6. This violates RULES R13, 'Missing means NaN, never a neighbour; a gap must fail closed', which predates this finding by many sessions.
THE TREATMENT, fixed now: an episode whose har_1h, har_6h or har_1d sits AT the floor is treated as having a MISSING trailing-window feature. The feature becomes NaN and the episode is dropped by the finite-row filter that already exists and already applies identically to every arm.
WHY THIS IS NOT OUTLIER REMOVAL, and the distinction is the whole point. The trigger is the INPUT (rv5 == 0, observable at prediction time), not the LOSS. It is decided by a rule written long before this episode was found. It applies to every arm identically. And it is detectable live: a serving system can see a zero-volume hour without knowing the outcome. Dropping episodes because a MODEL did badly on them would be indefensible; declining to forecast from an hour with no data is what the rule already required.
BOTH VERSIONS ARE REPORTED, ALWAYS. Every Phase 2 scorecard and every arm carries the floored and unfloored numbers side by side. If any Phase 2 conclusion differs between them, that difference is reported as the headline rather than resolved silently.
PHASE 1 IS NOT TOUCHED. Its artifacts are frozen and immutable. Its NUMBERS stand exactly as published. What changes is one INTERPRETATION: BENCHMARK.md and vol-matrix-fair-result read har_short's H=1 score of 1.03094 as overfitting five regressors to one horizon. That reading is wrong and is corrected -- the score is real, its cause is a data gap, and 0.201% of episodes carry the fault.
experiments.result: MEASURED. One episode = 72.5% of fold 2022's mean QLIKE at H=1; top ten = 78.9%; excluding them the fold scores 0.6000 against har_short's headline 2.83480 for that fold. Floor counts: har_1h 958 episodes (0.201%), har_6h 156, har_1d 115, har_5d 0, har_22d 0. Hourly bars with rv5 <= 0: 4,258 of 128,031, of which 3,520 have volume == 0. In the modern era only 11 bars, 10 zero-volume, across 2020/2022/2023/2024/2025.
experiments.implication:
THIS IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL SINGLE EPISODE IN THE PROJECT and it was found by asking why a baseline lost, not by asking why a model won. har_short is the teacher that beats NOCTUA at three of four horizons; the one horizon where it looked incompetent turns out to be one hour of missing exchange data in July 2022.
IT ALSO CHANGES WHAT THE 1h ROW MEANS. Phase 1 concluded 'NOCTUA does not beat a properly specified HAR family at any horizon', and that conclusion is UNCHANGED -- NOCTUA loses at H=1 to persistence and garch_t, neither of which is affected by this. But the specific claim that har_short overfits at H=1 is withdrawn.
AND IT IS A LIVE SERVING RISK, not only a research one. The same floor exists in the shipped feature path. A zero-volume hour before a violent move would produce a near-zero sigma forecast in production. That is recorded here and is a candidate for a shipped fix ON ITS OWN MERITS, separately from Phase 2, and is not adopted as part of any teacher experiment.
experiments.lesson:
A SENTINEL VALUE IS A LIE THE PIPELINE TELLS ITSELF. `max(rv, EPS)` was written to avoid log(0), which is a real problem, and it solved it by inventing a number. The number is not merely wrong, it is CONFIDENTLY wrong in the most dangerous direction: it asserts near-zero volatility, which is exactly what makes a linear model forecast near-zero sigma.
GENERALISED, and this is R43: when a guard against a numerical edge case substitutes a value, ask what that value CLAIMS. EPS in a log is not neutral -- it is the strongest possible statement the feature can make. Prefer NaN and let the row fail closed.

experiments.question: Is a calib-fitted scalar on NOCTUA's sigma adoptable as NOCTUA V2's first component?
experiments.rule:
PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE the adoption harness exists. The MECHANISM is already established by `M-noctua-scale-perfold`; this entry is the ADOPTION test, and passing the mechanism test is explicitly NOT passing this one.
WHY A SEPARATE ENTRY. `scale_falsifier.py` answered 'is NOCTUA's deficit a scale constant'. It did NOT answer 'should the shipped model change', and it cannot, because it reports pooled means and a within-arm gain interval rather than the paired per-episode contrast against the teacher, and because it never touched the barrier curves.
PRIMARY, per TEACHER_ZOO section 9: paired PER-EPISODE moving-block bootstrap, block max(n^(1/3), 2H), on the QLIKE difference between c*NOCTUA and THE BEST CALIB-SELECTED TEACHER AT THAT HORIZON, WITH THAT TEACHER ALSO RESCALED BY ITS OWN CALIB-FITTED c. Comparing a rescaled candidate against an unrescaled baseline would be R39 all over again -- the correction is available to every arm and must be given to every arm.
THE BARRIER CONDITION, INHERITED FROM `E-scale` AND NON-NEGOTIABLE. E-scale's own rule says: 'Must also re-score the barrier curves, since scaling sigma moves every touch probability, which a median-only re-weighting does not test.' That condition is unmet and R4 says the stricter written commitment governs. So: pinball, CRPS, Brier and the CORP decomposition at every barrier, plus Christoffersen conditional coverage, all re-scored under c. ADOPTION IS BLOCKED until they are, WHATEVER the QLIKE numbers say.
GUARDS, all must hold: (i) post-rescale calibration ratio within [0.95, 1.05] on TEST; (ii) no slice may degrade by more than 2% relative -- stated on BOTH slices per E-scale, never pooled; (iii) worst fold must not degrade; (iv) barrier discrimination (DSC) must not fall.
NEGATIVE CONTROLS: (a) a SHUFFLED-c control that assigns each fold a c drawn from a different fold, which must NOT reproduce the gain -- if it does, the gain is a global constant and not a fitted correction; (b) c fixed at 1.0, which must reproduce the unrescaled NOCTUA bit-identically.
FAMILY: joins the Phase 2 volatility family. 4 horizons x 1 primary = 4, Bonferroni within it.
REJECTION: if the paired CI against the rescaled best teacher contains zero at a horizon, the scalar has not been shown to beat that teacher there. If the barrier metrics degrade, the component is rejected for adoption regardless of QLIKE, because NOCTUA's product is a touch-probability curve and not a sigma.
experiments.result: pre-registered, not yet run
experiments.implication:
EXPECTED OUTCOME, recorded so it cannot be fitted afterwards.
I expect the QLIKE primary to CLEAR at H=6 and H=24, to be MARGINAL at H=1 (where the rescaled margin over garch_t is 0.0225, the largest of the three, but H=1 is also where calm degrades), and to FAIL at H=168 where NOCTUA loses to har_short by 0.0134 even after rescaling.
I am much less sure about the barriers, and that is the point of the condition. Scaling sigma up by ~1.2 moves EVERY touch probability up. NOCTUA's barrier curves were calibrated against the unscaled sigma, so the committee and the isotonic layer downstream have been fitted to absorb exactly the bias this correction removes. THE MOST LIKELY FAILURE MODE IS THAT QLIKE IMPROVES AND BRIER GETS WORSE, because the downstream calibration was silently compensating for the scale defect and now double-counts the fix. If that happens the honest conclusion is that the correction must be applied INSIDE the pipeline before Stage B rather than bolted onto the output -- which is a different and larger experiment, not a tweak to this one.

experiments.question: Is a calib-fitted scalar on NOCTUA's sigma adoptable as NOCTUA V2's first component?
experiments.rule: As pre-registered in P2-scale-v2, applied verbatim, including E-scale's inherited barrier condition.
experiments.result:
NOT ADOPTABLE. The QLIKE gain is real and large; EVERY barrier metric degrades; the pre-registered guards block adoption. Production slice, H=19 at 17:00 UTC, 2,046 test episodes, c fitted per fold on calib (mean 1.1377, fold spread 0.0646), applied through post_shift_fn so the correction reaches Stage B, the committee and every barrier.
  QLIKE pooled  0.29702 -> 0.26825   gain +0.02877 (9.7% relative), CI [+0.00924, +0.04889] which EXCLUDES ZERO favourably
  QLIKE spike   1.76571 -> 1.18202   a 33% improvement on the slice that matters most
  QLIKE calm    0.21917 -> 0.21981   essentially unchanged
  calib ratio   1.2662 -> 0.9759     the scale defect is fixed, and the guard band [0.95,1.05] is satisfied
AND THEN EVERY BARRIER METRIC GOES THE WRONG WAY:
  DSC     0.009086 -> 0.007799   -14.16%   (discrimination, the uncheatable one)
  MCB     0.024738 -> 0.026836    +8.48%   (miscalibration, lower is better)
  brier   0.180098 -> 0.183483    +1.88%
  crps    0.005251 -> 0.005460    +3.99%
  logs    0.527487 -> 0.536268    +1.66%
  pinball 0.003577 -> 0.003705    +3.59%
GUARDS: ratio_in_band PASS, spike_not_worse PASS, calm_not_worse PASS, dsc_not_worse FAIL, brier_not_worse FAIL. Two of five fail, so the verdict is REJECT for adoption regardless of the QLIKE interval.
experiments.implication:
THE PRE-REGISTERED EXPECTATION NAMED THIS OUTCOME BEFORE THE RUN, which is the only reason it reads as a measurement rather than as a rescue. P2-scale-v2 recorded: 'THE MOST LIKELY FAILURE MODE IS THAT QLIKE IMPROVES AND BRIER GETS WORSE.' It did, on all six barrier metrics.
WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES, and it is worth more than an adoption would have been: THE SCALE THAT MINIMISES QLIKE IS NOT THE SCALE THAT PLACES THE BARRIER QUANTILES. Those are different functionals of the same distribution. QLIKE is minimised by the conditional MEAN of variance; a touch probability depends on where the quantiles sit relative to a fixed barrier. Multiplying the whole distribution by 1.14 moves the mean into place and drags every quantile with it.
THE MECHANISM I BELIEVE, STATED AS A HYPOTHESIS AND NOT AS ESTABLISHED, because I have been wrong about a mechanism already this phase: NOCTUA reports sigma_med, a MEDIAN, and the barrier machinery was built around a median-centred distribution. The QLIKE deficit is a mean-vs-median mismatch. You cannot repair a mean-median gap by scaling, because scaling moves both by the same factor. The correction needed is a SHAPE change -- more right-tail mass without displacing the median -- not a multiplicative one.
FALSIFIER FOR THAT HYPOTHESIS, pre-registered here: apply a correction that inflates the upper quantiles while holding the median fixed, and check whether QLIKE improves WITHOUT the barrier metrics degrading. If the barriers still degrade, the explanation is wrong and the problem is not the median at all.
E-scale IS NOW CLOSED, after being open since Phase 0. Its question was 'should NOCTUA's point forecast be scaled up from the median toward the QLIKE-optimal mean'. The answer is NO -- not by scaling. Its own barrier condition, which is why it was never closed on QLIKE evidence alone, is what produced the answer.
experiments.lesson:
A CONDITION WRITTEN INTO A PRE-REGISTRATION AND THEN LEFT UNMET FOR THREE PHASES IS STILL THE RULE. E-scale said in Phase 0 that the barrier curves must be re-scored because scaling sigma moves every touch probability. Every QLIKE result since has pointed at adopting the scale fix, and the scorecard, the overlay and the falsifier all independently found the under-forecast signature. It would have been easy to treat the barrier clause as bureaucracy. It is the clause that produced the correct answer, and it reversed a decision that four separate lines of evidence supported.
GENERALISED, R45: when a candidate improves the metric you optimise and you have a SECOND metric that represents the actual product, the second one is not a formality -- it is the one that knows whether you improved the thing or the proxy.

experiments.question: Can NOCTUA learn only the residual of a cross-fitted teacher, and does that beat the teacher itself?
experiments.rule: As pre-registered in P2-armA-residual, applied verbatim. Sign convention: positive = arm better than its teacher; the CI must exclude zero favourably.
experiments.result:
A1 CLEARS AT THREE OF FOUR HORIZONS. A3 CLEARS NOWHERE. The pre-registered prediction held on both counts.
  H=1    A1 0.79143 vs har_short +0.23951 CI [+0.01280, +1.01997] CLEARS -- but see below, this is a rescue of a broken teacher and A1 is still WORSE than A0 from scratch (0.72068).
         A2 0.66644 vs garch_t -0.09206 CI [-0.11454, -0.07084] WORSE, excludes zero adversely.
         A3 0.72486 vs garch_t -0.15048 CI [-0.19107, -0.11633] WORSE.
  H=6    A1 0.39020 vs har_short +0.02690 CI [+0.01827, +0.03816] CLEARS, and BEATS the calib-best teacher garch_t both raw (0.41246) and rescaled (0.41073).
         A2 -0.00682 and A3 -0.00187 both straddle zero.
  H=24   A1 = A2 (har_short is the calib-best teacher) 0.25835 vs +0.01984 CI [+0.00942, +0.02953] CLEARS. Beats raw har_short 0.27818, does NOT beat rescaled har_short 0.25696.
         A3 +0.00740 CI [-0.00450, +0.01800] does not clear.
  H=168  A1 = A2 -0.00636 CI [-0.03132, +0.01592] does not clear, and is worse than A0 (0.17410). A3 +0.00251 does not clear. At this horizon A0 from scratch beats every teacher.
THE DECOMPOSITION IS THE RESULT, and it answers the concern that motivated adding it. The residual's gain is NOT a level correction:
  H=6  constant part -0.01827 of a +0.02690 total = -68%.  implied c=0.979, residual sd=0.071
  H=24 constant part -0.01379 of a +0.01984 total = -70%.  implied c=0.976, residual sd=0.081
The constant part is NEGATIVE. Applying only the mean residual would make the teacher WORSE; every bit of the improvement, and then some, comes from the EPISODE-VARYING part. And the implied c of 0.976-0.979 points slightly DOWNWARD, the opposite direction from the 1.112-1.213 the scale falsifier fitted. Arm A is not re-deriving the scalar that P2-scale-v2 rejected; it is a different mechanism.
experiments.implication:
THE PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION ABOUT A3 WAS THE SHARP ONE AND IT HELD. I wrote that A3 should help LESS than A1/A2 'because a feature column can be ignored or diluted by the network while an additive offset cannot'. A3 clears at ZERO horizons and is significantly WORSE than its teacher at H=1. So the teacher's forecast as information is nearly worthless to NOCTUA; the DECOMPOSITION is what carries the result. That is a statement about inductive bias, not about data, and it is the most transferable thing Phase 2 has produced.
WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and matters for adoption. At H=24 A1 beats RAW har_short but not har_short with its own calib-fitted scalar (0.25835 against 0.25696). Under R39 the baseline is entitled to that correction, so H=24 is NOT a win over a properly equipped teacher. Only H=6 beats the calib-best teacher on both raw and rescaled terms.
THE HORIZON PATTERN IS COHERENT AND WORTH STATING. At H=1 the teacher is either broken (har_short) or already optimal (garch_t), and the residual helps in the first case and hurts in the second -- consistent with the residual having nothing to add to a well-scaled teacher. At H=168 A0 from scratch beats every teacher AND every residual arm, so there is nothing to decompose onto. The residual architecture pays off in the middle, where the teacher is good but not optimal.
BARRIERS ARE NOT YET SCORED for Arm A. P2-scale-v2 established that a QLIKE gain on this model can coexist with across-the-board barrier degradation, so no Arm A adoption claim is available until the same barrier battery runs. That is the next gate, not a formality.
experiments.lesson: ADDING THE DECOMPOSITION BEFORE THE RUN, BECAUSE THE SMOKE TEST MADE ME SUSPICIOUS, IS WHAT MADE THIS INTERPRETABLE. The smoke number (0.25760 at H=24) sat almost exactly on the rescaled har_short (0.25696), which looked like the residual model quietly re-deriving a constant that had just been rejected. It is not: the constant part is NEGATIVE at both horizons where the arm clears. Without the split I would have had a clean pass and no way to tell the two stories apart, and the coincidence would have gone unexamined.

experiments.question: What is the model actually fed, is it event-labelled, and what does that cost?
experiments.rule: A forensic audit, not a pre-registered experiment: every claim measured from artifacts and stated with its number, and every hypothesis I formed tested rather than asserted.
experiments.result:
NO EVENT LABELS EXIST. All 42 model inputs derive from OHLCV plus the clock. The single binary `reg_post_etf`, which flips once in Jan 2024, is the entire extent of world-knowledge. data/news.json holds 14 LIVE headlines, not a corpus; data/fg.json a single current value. DVOL (36.9% coverage, 62,204 training rows) and funding (50.0%, 128,780) exist in the repo and are NOT wired in. No macro calendar, no flows, no order book, no on-chain, no sentiment.
ERROR IS EXTREMELY CONCENTRATED: the worst 5% of episodes carry 52.8% of NOCTUA's pooled QLIKE at H=1, 52.0% at H=24, and 76.0% of har_short's at H=1. The worst 0.1% carry 48.0% of har_short's at H=1. garch_t is the LEAST concentrated (37.7% at H=1, 16.6% at H=168), which is the mechanism behind its spike advantage -- it over-reacts and is less often caught flat.
DATA INTEGRITY: `filled` is 0 across all 7,681,837 minutes -- no synthetic bars. bad_print 0.15%, 52 modern hours. Zero-volume minutes 17.08% overall, 94.95% (2012) to 0.48% (2026), varying 8x ACROSS TEST FOLDS.
A HYPOTHESIS OF MINE, FALSIFIED: I predicted dead minutes bias rv5 downward. Against Parkinson's range estimator the ratio rv5/Parkinson RISES with dead-minute density (1.15 -> 1.90, Spearman +0.119) instead of falling. Quiet markets genuinely have low vol. But the test exposed that two standard estimators of the SAME target disagree by 15-90%, and only one has ever been used.
experiments.implication:
THE ASYMMETRY IS THE POINT AND IT IS NOT INTUITIVE. Event data would plausibly help VOLATILITY and would mostly NOT help DIRECTION, so 'label the events' is a fix for one of the two failures.
For volatility: scheduled macro announcements are a known forecastable driver, the schedule is public in advance so there is no look-ahead risk, and half the error sits in the 5% of episodes such a calendar would flag. This is the highest value-per-unit-risk item available.
For direction: by the time news is public it is priced. D1 measured 8 of 8 arms failing at n~49,000 with calibration slopes of -0.03 to +0.06. A news feed there adds look-ahead risk -- published timestamps are unreliable -- against a measured near-zero signal.
experiments.lesson: I FORMED A DATA-QUALITY HYPOTHESIS AND IT WAS WRONG, AND TESTING IT WAS STILL THE RIGHT CALL: the falsification surfaced the estimator-disagreement finding, which is more important than the hypothesis would have been. Auditing a dataset means measuring the things you suspect AND reporting when the suspicion fails.

experiments.question: Do scheduled clock-anchored events drive the concentrated forecast error, and can that be tested without acquiring an event calendar?
experiments.rule: A hypothesis test designed to need NO new data. If scheduled macro releases drive the extreme errors, the worst episodes must cluster at the UTC hours those releases occur. If the worst episodes are uniform across anchor hours, a calendar cannot help through this channel and the audit's top recommendation is wrong. OMNIBUS TEST: chi-square of the worst-5% anchor-hour distribution against the anchor-hour distribution of ALL episodes -- so the per-hour lifts are descriptive and the verdict does not rest on picking the largest of 24.
experiments.result:
CONFIRMED AT H=1, ABSENT AT H=24, AND THE CONTRAST IS THE FINDING.
  H=1  chi-square 324.7, p = 4.5e-55. Overwhelmingly non-uniform. Worst-5% lift by UTC anchor hour: 14:00 = 1.788, 18:00 = 1.533, 19:00 = 1.465, 13:00 = 1.201, and the MINIMUM is 11:00 at 0.440. 14:00 UTC contains the 14:30 US equity cash open; 13:00 contains the 13:30 CPI/NFP/PPI print; 18:00-19:00 brackets the 19:00 FOMC statement.
  H=24 chi-square 3.0, p = 1.000. Perfectly uniform. Lifts span 0.928 to 1.055.
The H=24 null is not a failure of the hypothesis -- it is the CONTROL working. A 24-hour window contains every hour of the day, so the anchor hour carries no information about which events fall inside it. Finding clustering there would have indicated a bug.
AND THE MODEL CANNOT REPRESENT WHAT WAS FOUND. Its only hour-of-day inputs are cal_hour_sin and cal_hour_cos -- a SINGLE Fourier harmonic, one maximum per 24 hours. The observed shape has a 4.06x swing between 11:00 and 14:00 three hours apart AND a second elevated shoulder at 18:00-19:00. Spectrally, harmonic 1 carries 44.1% of the power and harmonics 2-6 carry 43.7%. Half the intraday structure is invisible to the basis.
experiments.implication:
THE AUDIT'S TOP RECOMMENDATION IS PARTLY RIGHT AND PARTLY REDUNDANT, and the test that distinguished them cost nothing.
RIGHT: scheduled clock-anchored events measurably drive extreme 1-hour errors. The footprint is at exactly the hours US macro and the equity open occur.
REDUNDANT AT LONG HORIZONS: at H=24 the anchor hour is uninformative by construction, so a calendar cannot help through this channel. It would have to encode 'is an FOMC INSIDE this window', which is a different feature that this test cannot evaluate and that remains open.
AND THERE IS A CHEAPER FIX AVAILABLE FIRST. Half the intraday structure is unrepresentable in the current basis. Adding hour-of-day dummies or higher harmonics needs NO EXTERNAL DATA, no provenance chain, and carries no look-ahead risk whatsoever -- the clock is known in advance. That should be tested BEFORE investing in calendar acquisition, because if it captures most of the effect the calendar's marginal value drops sharply.
INFRASTRUCTURE NOTE: federalreserve.gov is EGRESS BLOCKED, so an authoritative FOMC calendar cannot currently be fetched. Secondary sources returned partial dates. Building a feature on unverified secondary dates would violate R14 -- read boundaries from the source, do not type plausible ones -- so no calendar has been constructed.
experiments.lesson: TEST THE HYPOTHESIS WITH THE DATA YOU HAVE BEFORE BUYING THE DATA YOU WANT. The audit recommended acquiring a macro calendar. Before acquiring anything, the FOOTPRINT of scheduled events was measurable from anchor timestamps alone -- and it both confirmed the hypothesis at H=1, refuted its relevance at H=24, and surfaced a cheaper fix that needs no external data at all. The acquisition would have been justified either way; it would also have been the third priority rather than the first.

experiments.question: Does a richer hour-of-day basis capture the intraday error structure the single Fourier harmonic cannot represent?
experiments.rule:
PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE the harness exists.
MOTIVATION, measured in P2-event-footprint and not assumed: the worst-5% episodes at H=1 cluster by UTC anchor hour with chi-square 324.7, p=4.5e-55, lift 1.788 at 14:00 against 0.440 at 11:00, and a second shoulder at 18:00-19:00. The model's only hour-of-day inputs are cal_hour_sin and cal_hour_cos -- ONE harmonic, one maximum per day -- which carries 44.1% of the observed spectral power while harmonics 2-6 carry 43.7%.
TREATMENT: replace the two calendar columns with a richer basis. Two arms, both declared now: (B1) harmonics 1-3 (six columns, sin/cos at periods 24, 12, 8 hours); (B2) 23 hour-of-day dummies. Everything else held fixed -- same episodes, folds, embargo, seeds, target, QLIKE, paired per-episode primary with the 2H block length.
PRIMARY: paired PER-EPISODE moving-block bootstrap on the QLIKE difference against the UNCHANGED basis, at each horizon.
FAMILY: 2 arms x 4 horizons = 8, Bonferroni within it. Failed cells stay in the family.
POWER, stated before the fact per R5: the FOLD-LEVEL MDE at 80% power is 18.89% of base at H=1 and 19.17% at H=6. No plausible calendar-basis effect is that large, so THE FOLD-LEVEL COMPARISON IS A NON-MEASUREMENT AND IS LABELLED NOT POWERED BEFORE IT RUNS. Only the per-episode estimator can resolve this, which is why it is the primary.
GUARD, and it is the one that matters: this treatment adds CALENDAR columns, which are known in advance and cannot leak. But it also adds capacity. A negative control is therefore mandatory -- a SHUFFLED-HOUR arm where the hour label is permuted across episodes. It must NOT improve on the unchanged basis. If it does, the gain is capacity rather than clock information and both arms are rejected.
REJECTION: if the paired CI contains zero at a horizon, the richer basis has not been shown to help there. Barriers are NOT scored in this entry and no adoption follows from it -- P2-scale-v2-result established that a QLIKE gain on this model can coexist with across-the-board barrier degradation.
experiments.result: pre-registered, not yet run
experiments.implication:
EXPECTED OUTCOME, recorded so it cannot be fitted afterwards.
I expect a clear gain at H=1, a smaller one at H=6, and NOTHING at H=24 and H=168. The reasoning is the same structural fact that made P2-event-footprint's H=24 result a control rather than a failure: a 24-hour window contains every hour, so the anchor hour cannot tell the model which part of the day the forward window covers. If H=24 or H=168 DOES improve, my explanation is wrong and the gain is coming from something other than intraday timing -- most likely raw capacity, which is exactly what the shuffled-hour control is there to detect.
I also expect B2 (dummies) to beat B1 (three harmonics), because the observed shape has a sharp three-hour swing that even three harmonics smooth over. If B1 matches B2, the effect is smoother than the lift table suggested.

experiments.question: Does Arm A's H=6 QLIKE gain survive the barrier battery when the residual architecture runs through the SHIPPED pipeline?
experiments.rule:
PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE THE HARNESS RUNS. P2-armA-result closed with an explicit gate: 'BARRIERS ARE NOT YET SCORED for Arm A... no Arm A adoption claim is available until the same barrier battery runs. That is the next gate, not a formality.' This is that gate, and the battery is P2-scale-v2's, unchanged, because a battery redesigned after seeing which arm is being tested is not a battery.
SCOPE. H=6 ONLY. It is the single cell of the twelve that beat its calib-best teacher both raw and rescaled; H=24 beat raw har_short but not rescaled har_short and is therefore not a win over a properly equipped teacher (R39), and H=1/H=168 did not clear. Running the battery on cells that already failed the QLIKE primary would be shopping.
ARCHITECTURE, THROUGH run_fold AND NOT BESIDE IT. `benchmark.run_fold` gains a `residual_anchor` argument: the network and the blend anchor are both fitted on y - anchor, and the anchor is added back through the EXISTING `post_shift_fn` hook, which puts it in front of Stage B, the committee and every barrier. That routing is the entire point -- eval/arm_a_residual.py scored QLIKE in its own loop and structurally could not say what the decomposition does to a touch probability. Reimplementing the scoring here instead would be R18's mistake. run_fold's existing assertion that the achieved log-level shift equals the requested one to 1e-6 is retained and is a pass condition.
THE ANCHOR IS CROSS-FITTED, AND NOT READ FROM teacher_oof.npz. That artifact is built on episodes_h4; run_fold trains on the MAIN episodes table (H in {6,12,19,24}) and calibrates its committee on H=19, so the artifact cannot supply the values this pipeline needs. har_short is therefore refitted under the SAME rule: TRAIN-slice values come from `teacher_zoo.inner_oof` expanding-forward (TEACHER_ZOO Amendment 1, block 1 left NaN and DROPPED, never filled); calib- and test-slice values come from a fit on that fold's train slice only. assert_slices_disjoint and assert_causal_boundary are called per fold. A VALIDATION is required and is a pass condition: on the H=6 test slice the refitted anchor must reproduce teacher_oof.npz's har_short sigma to 1e-9 on the anchor timestamps common to both tables. If it does not, this is a different teacher than the one P2-armA-result measured and the run is void.
