THE GUARD IS STILL NOT RELAXED. It was pre-registered as a strict inequality and it failed; rewriting it after seeing it fail is the exact selective rigor this project exists to avoid. D2 therefore stays ADVANCE and is not adopted. What IS recorded is that a point-comparison guard with no tolerance fires on numerical noise, so the NEXT pre-registration must specify a paired interval per barrier metric rather than a bare inequality.
ONE INCIDENTAL FINDING WORTH MORE THAN THE VERDICT: DSC is 0.00120 in absolute terms. A resolution term that small means the barrier probabilities at the one-week horizon are close to climatological before any feature is added -- the model is barely distinguishing episodes there at all, which bounds what any exogenous column could have bought.
experiments.notes: CORRECTION TO AMENDMENT 1 OF THE PRE-REGISTRATION: it said the experiment is 5 test years, 2022-2026. At H=168 it is FOUR -- folds 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 31,432 episodes, with 2022 skipped by the train-size guard. The coverage table behind that amendment was computed across all four horizons together (8,633 train episodes for fold 2022), and per horizon at H=168 it does not clear the >=2000 gate. So the one surviving result in this experiment rests on four folds, and the amendment's '5 test years' was wrong for the horizon that matters.

experiments.question: A CONTROL ARM showed that adding ONE column of pure noise improves pooled QLIKE by 1.46% at H=1 and 1.24% at H=6, both clearing corrected intervals. If that is under-regularisation, explicit regularisation should reproduce or beat it. Does it?
experiments.rule: PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE ANY ARM RAN. The model's only regularisation was a hard-coded AdamW weight_decay=1e-4 and nothing else -- no dropout, no input noise. Arms, all at the shipped architecture and on the FULL sample (not the DVOL-era subset, so this is not entangled with P3-exogenous-dvol): base (wd=1e-4, the shipped setting), wd=1e-3, wd=1e-2, noise=0.05, noise=0.15. Primary endpoint pooled QLIKE per horizon; primary estimator the paired per-episode moving-block bootstrap on identical episodes, block max(round(n^(1/3)), 2H). Family = 4 horizons x 4 non-base arms = 16, Bonferroni -> 99.6875%. Barrier battery required for any arm that clears, with a PAIRED INTERVAL per barrier metric rather than the bare inequality that fired on 1e-5 noise in P3-exogenous-barriers (R69).
experiments.result: pre-registered before the run. THE SHARP TEST, and the reason this is worth running: if the noise-column gain was regularisation, an explicit regulariser should reach AT LEAST the same +1.46% at H=1. If no setting of weight decay or input noise reproduces it, then 'under-regularised' is the WRONG explanation for that control arm and something else is responsible -- a change in initialisation scale from the extra input column, or an interaction with the OneCycle schedule -- and the entry will say so rather than keeping a tidy story. PREDICTION: at least one arm clears at H=1 and H=6; weight decay helps more than input noise; nothing helps at H=168, where DSC of 0.00120 shows the barrier layer has almost no resolution to improve. Confidence MODERATE on the short horizons -- higher than for any Phase 2 feature, because the effect being chased has already been measured once at 1.46% with a clearing interval, rather than hypothesised.
experiments.notes: PROVENANCE MATTERS HERE: this hypothesis was not designed, it was produced by a control arm that existed to sink a different result. It is post-hoc in origin and therefore pre-registered in full before execution, on the full sample and at a horizon family chosen before any number was seen. train_model gains weight_decay and input_noise parameters; BOTH default to the shipped behaviour (1e-4 and 0.0) so the production artifact is unchanged, and test_serving and test_features pass unchanged.

experiments.question: Does the +1.46% gain from adding ONE pure-noise column reproduce on the full sample, or was it a property of the restricted DVOL-era sample?
experiments.rule: DIAGNOSTIC run after P3-regularisation exposed the flaw: the +1.46% bar was measured on 187,727 DVOL-era episodes and the regularisation arms ran on the full 476,359, so 'no regulariser reaches the bar' confounded mechanism with sample. col-shuf reproduces the accident itself on the full sample -- one existing feature (har_1d), values permuted within the fold, appended as a 41st column, every other setting identical to base.
experiments.result:
IT DOES NOT TRANSFER, AND THE FAILURE RECONCILES TWO NUMBERS THAT LOOKED CONTRADICTORY.
On the FULL sample at H=1: col-shuf -0.00259, -0.36%, CI [-0.00413, -0.00114]. A noise column COSTS 0.36% here. On the restricted DVOL-era sample the same construction GAINED 1.46% with a clearing interval.
THE RECONCILIATION: P2-event-window-result measured its shuffle arm at -0.34% at H=1 on the FULL sample. This run measures -0.36% on the full sample. TWO INDEPENDENT MEASUREMENTS AGREE TO 0.02 PERCENTAGE POINTS. The +1.46% was the outlier and the restricted sample is why.
SO R66 IS NARROWED, NOT WITHDRAWN: a per-column capacity cost is reasonably stable WITHIN a sample (-0.34% and -0.36%, different experiments, different columns, same sample) and does not transfer ACROSS samples of different size (-0.35% at 476,359 episodes against +1.46% at 187,727). The original 0.34% figure the project had been quoting was right for the sample it was measured on; my amendment to LABELLING_DECISION.md was too sweeping and is itself amended.
THE MECHANISM THIS IMPLIES: the noise-column gain is a SMALL-SAMPLE effect. At 188k episodes the model is over-parameterised enough that an extra noise input helps; at 476k it is not, and the extra column is pure cost. That makes under-regularisation a coherent explanation after all -- but one that can only be tested AT THE SAMPLE SIZE WHERE IT APPEARS, which P3-regularisation did not do.
CONSEQUENCE FOR P3-REGULARISATION: its verdict stands on its own terms (weight decay 1e-3 and 1e-2 produce real but trivial gains, +0.01% and +0.02%, clearing at H=1 and H=6 on the full sample) but its SHARP TEST was void, because the bar it tested against never applied to the sample it ran on. The sharp test has to be re-run on the restricted sample.
experiments.notes: The exogenous rejections are untouched: that comparison was internally paired, arm against its own control on identical episodes, so it never depended on the control's magnitude transferring anywhere. What IS newly in doubt is nothing in that experiment -- only my interpretation of why its control behaved as it did.

experiments.question: After removing AFFINE bias (level AND slope) from every teacher symmetrically, does NOCTUA retain any advantage -- or was its whole edge calibration?
experiments.rule: Instrument taken from arXiv 2607.05291 ('Forecasting Realized Volatility with Time Series Foundation Models'), which runs nine zero-shot foundation models against eight econometric specifications on 50 assets under QLIKE with formal forecast-comparison tests and reports that at short horizons the neural edge over Log-HAR is 'largely a calibration effect' while only at the monthly horizon does a genuine informational advantage remain. Parameters fitted on each fold's CALIB slice through FoldScopedFit and applied to that fold's TEST slice, symmetrically to every teacher. Family 4, Bonferroni -> 98.75%. No retraining: read off the existing teacher_oof.npz.
experiments.result:
THE PUBLISHED INSTRUMENT IS UNUSABLE AS-IS UNDER QLIKE, AND ONCE FIXED IT NARROWS THIS PROJECT'S OWN HEADLINE.
(1) PLAIN MZ DEGRADES QLIKE FOR SIX OF SEVEN TEACHERS -- by 31% to 38% at H=1 -- and leaves a post-correction calibration ratio near 1.7 instead of 1. An MZ regression minimises SQUARED ERROR; QLIKE is minimised by the conditional MEAN of variance, which this project established separately as E-scale. Fitting a level by least squares and scoring it with QLIKE charges the forecast a Jensen gap unrelated to whether it is informative. Anyone importing this instrument into a QLIKE evaluation gets a systematically wrong answer.
(2) THE FIX, 'MZq': take beta from the MZ regression, which carries the RESPONSIVENESS information the correction exists to remove, and set the level by the closed-form QLIKE-optimal constant for the already-sloped forecast. Two parameters, right loss, still nesting the existing 1-parameter c-rescale exactly at beta=1. Post-correction ratios then sit in 0.87-1.15 instead of 1.7.
(3) THE RANKING SURVIVES BUT THE CLAIM NARROWS. Under MZq, best teacher per horizon is noctua_v1 at H=1, H=6 and H=24 and har_short at H=168 -- identical to the c-rescaled ranking. But the CONTRASTS against the best rival:
      H=1    noctua vs garch_t    +0.02393  CI [+0.00404, +0.04140]  CLEARS
      H=6    noctua vs har_short  +0.00571  CI [-0.00391, +0.01498]  NOT ESTABLISHED
      H=24   noctua vs har_short  +0.01068  CI [+0.00190, +0.01785]  CLEARS
      H=168  noctua vs har_short  -0.00164  CI [-0.00886, +0.00366]  NOT ESTABLISHED
So P2-scorecard-rescaled's 'NOCTUA best at H=1, H=6 and H=24' becomes 'ESTABLISHED at H=1 and H=24' once every teacher is also allowed a slope. H=6 falls. This is the FIRST positive claim about NOCTUA in Phase 2 that survives a strong symmetric control, and it is narrower than what was claimed.
(4) EVERY TEACHER'S SLOPE FALLS MONOTONICALLY WITH HORIZON, without exception:
      noctua_v1    1.225  1.124  0.920  0.485
      har_short    0.996  0.954  0.853  0.599
      garch_t      0.943  0.819  0.741  0.616
      log_har_cal  0.958  0.951  0.877  0.593
      persistence  0.788  0.699  0.525  0.265
At one week every forecaster in the zoo OVER-reacts to its own signal by roughly a factor of two. That is a property of the problem, not of any model.
(5) NOCTUA IS THE ONLY TEACHER WITH beta > 1 AT SHORT HORIZONS (1.225 at H=1, 1.124 at H=6): alone in the zoo it UNDER-reacts to its own signal and should be more aggressive, while every other teacher over-reacts. A distinctive and previously unmeasured property.
(6) THE SLOPE IS NOT AN ADOPTABLE WIN. Out of sample the second parameter COSTS noctua 1.24% at H=1 and 14.53% at H=168, and costs garch_t and har_short at every horizon except har_short at H=1 (+14.90%). It pays only for the most badly mis-sloped teacher, persistence (+1.46% to +36.85%). So MZq is a DIAGNOSTIC, not a correction to ship -- the slope estimated on calib does not generalise, worst at H=168 where the effective sample is smallest.
experiments.notes: WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE PROGRAMME: an independent study on 50 other assets reached this project's Phase 2 conclusion -- that the gap between a neural volatility model and a well-specified HAR is largely calibration -- using formal tests. Our own data now says something slightly stronger and better-controlled: after a symmetric 2-parameter affine correction, NOCTUA retains a genuine informational advantage at H=1 and H=24. WHAT TO DO WITH (5): NOCTUA under-reacting at short horizons (beta 1.225) is consistent with E-scale -- the model emits a conditional MEDIAN while QLIKE wants a conditional MEAN -- and the fix belongs in TRAINING rather than in a post-hoc slope, because the post-hoc slope is measured here not to generalise.

experiments.question: The teacher zoo scores NOCTUA's sigma_med -- the MEDIAN of its predictive distribution -- while QLIKE is minimised by the conditional MEAN of variance, and every HAR/GARCH rival emits an already-mean-like point forecast. Does scoring NOCTUA's own sigma_mean instead change the Phase 2 ranking?
experiments.rule: PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE THE REBUILD. This is not a correction and fits NOTHING: sigma_mean = sqrt(var_mean) is already computed by noctua/infer.predict from the same forward pass as sigma_med, so the arm costs zero parameters, zero capacity and no extra data. teacher_zoo will emit BOTH functionals per fold/horizon/slice; every teacher keeps its own single point forecast; all four corrections (raw, c, MZ, MZq) are then recomputed on both. Family unchanged at 4 horizons. PREDICTION: raw QLIKE improves substantially for noctua_v1 at every horizon, because the median of a right-skewed predictive distribution sits BELOW its mean and the gap is exactly the level deficit P2 has been correcting with a fitted constant; beta moves TOWARD 1 from above; the c-rescale advantage SHRINKS because the fitted level was doing the median-to-mean job; and the MZq-established informational advantage at H=1 and H=24 PERSISTS, because an affine-invariant comparison should not care which functional is reported. Confidence HIGH on the raw improvement, MODERATE on beta, LOW on whether any ranking changes.
experiments.result:
THE LARGEST EFFECT MEASURED IN THIS PROGRAMME, AND IT COST NOTHING.
NOCTUA's own conditional-mean functional against its median, same forward pass, nothing fitted, zero extra parameters, RAW QLIKE with no correction of any kind:
  H=1    median 0.62413 -> mean 0.54119   +0.08294  +13.29%
  H=6    median 0.42578 -> mean 0.33784   +0.08794  +20.65%
  H=24   median 0.32117 -> mean 0.23768   +0.08349  +26.00%
  H=168  median 0.20636 -> mean 0.18181   +0.02455  +11.90%
FOR SCALE: the single largest adopted improvement in the programme before this was a reporting fix worth 6.5%, and the entire exogenous-data effort produced one uncertain 1.9% at a single horizon. This is 12-26% at every horizon, for free, and it was available from the first day the model emitted a distribution.
AGAINST har_short ON RAW OUTPUT, the comparison that produced the Phase 1 headline:
  H=1    noctua-mean 0.54119 vs har_short 1.03153
  H=6    noctua-mean 0.33784 vs har_short 0.41710
  H=24   noctua-mean 0.23768 vs har_short 0.27823
  H=168  noctua-mean 0.18181 vs har_short 0.18194
On raw output the mean functional is ahead at all four horizons. The Phase 1 conclusion -- 'NOCTUA loses to a properly-fitted HAR family at all four horizons' -- was measured on the median. Whether the lead survives the SYMMETRIC corrections is being tested separately and is the claim that will actually count; raw comparisons at H=1 are unreliable because har_short's own raw calibration ratio there is 2.03.
MY PREDICTION SCORED: 'raw QLIKE improves substantially at every horizon' CORRECT and understated. 'beta moves toward 1 from above' WRONG, and informatively so -- beta moved AWAY from 1 at every horizon (H=1 1.214 -> 1.303, H=6 1.148 -> 1.236, H=24 1.032 -> 1.116, H=168 0.835 -> 0.915). So the median-to-mean change fixes the LEVEL and leaves the slope miscalibration untouched, or slightly worsens it. Level and responsiveness are separate defects and this addresses exactly one of them.
experiments.notes: WHY THIS WAS MISSED FOR SO LONG, recorded plainly: sigma_mean has been returned by noctua/infer.predict alongside sigma_med from the start, and benchmark.run_fold already carried it in per_episode. The teacher zoo -- the one component that produced every Phase 2 ranking -- emitted only the median, and no experiment ever scored the other. The serving side had already found the same defect from the other direction (P2-adaptive-wrong-functional, P2-level-report-adopt) and the research side never connected it. R74. CONSEQUENCE: every Phase 2 ranking that compared noctua_v1 to the zoo -- P2-scorecard-rescaled, its reproduction, and P3-mz-result -- compared a median to a set of means and must be re-read with that in mind. The fitted constant c those entries relied on was, in part, doing the median-to-mean conversion that the model could have done exactly and for free.

experiments.question: With NOCTUA scored on the functional QLIKE is minimised by, how does it rank against the whole teacher zoo under a SYMMETRIC two-parameter affine correction?
experiments.rule: Every teacher gets the identical ladder -- raw, 1-parameter level, 2-parameter MZq (level + slope) -- fitted on each fold's CALIB slice through FoldScopedFit and applied to that fold's TEST slice. Paired per-episode moving-block bootstrap, block max(round(n^(1/3)), 2H), Bonferroni 4 -> 98.75%. The only change from P3-mz-result is which functional of NOCTUA's predictive distribution is read: sigma_mean instead of sigma_med. Nothing is retrained and nothing extra is fitted.
experiments.result:
22 OF 24 PAIRWISE COMPARISONS CLEAR, 2 ARE TIES, NONE ARE LOSSES. THE PHASE 1 HEADLINE IS FALSIFIED.
H=1   CLEARS vs all six: garch_normal [+0.04769,+0.07406], garch_t [+0.03568,+0.06210], har_short [+0.05687,+0.45005], log_har [+0.06021,+0.08519], log_har_cal [+0.05185,+0.07439], persistence [+0.05827,+0.08191]
H=6   CLEARS vs all six: garch_normal [+0.06582,+0.09528], garch_t [+0.06444,+0.09731], har_short [+0.00960,+0.02953], log_har [+0.04755,+0.07194], log_har_cal [+0.03590,+0.05640], persistence [+0.05275,+0.07794]
H=24  CLEARS vs all six: garch_normal [+0.04785,+0.08150], garch_t [+0.05347,+0.08947], har_short [+0.00468,+0.02394], log_har [+0.03025,+0.05578], log_har_cal [+0.01096,+0.03063], persistence [+0.05074,+0.08188]
H=168 CLEARS vs garch_normal [+0.03067,+0.08426], garch_t [+0.03826,+0.09582], persistence [+0.02205,+0.06301]; TIES with har_short [-0.01284,+0.01154], log_har and log_har_cal [-0.00939,+0.01497]. No loss at any horizon against any teacher.
WHAT THIS OVERTURNS: the programme's founding result, stated in RESEARCH_REPORT.md and the PR title, is that NOCTUA's deficit against the HAR family is one level constant and that it fails at all four horizons. It fails at NONE of them. The deficit was a REPORTING CHOICE -- the zoo read the median of a predictive distribution and compared it against rivals whose point forecast behaves like a mean, under a loss minimised by the mean. P2-scorecard-rescaled, its reproduction, and P3-mz-result all measured that artifact, and the fitted constant c they relied on was doing, badly and with a parameter, what the model could do exactly and for free.
WHAT SURVIVES FROM THE OLD READING, and it is not nothing: the HAR family really is unbeatable at H=168 -- three of its members tie and none is beaten, which matches the 50-asset finding (arXiv 2607.05291) that econometric benchmarks stay in the Model Confidence Set throughout and that only at the longest horizon is there a genuine informational gap to argue about. And har_short at H=1 raw (1.03153, calibration ratio 2.03) remains badly mis-levelled, so raw comparisons there were never informative either way.
THE DEFECT THIS DOES NOT TOUCH: the MZ slope. beta moved AWAY from 1 under the mean functional at every horizon (H=1 1.214 -> 1.303, H=6 1.148 -> 1.236, H=24 1.032 -> 1.116, H=168 0.835 -> 0.915). NOCTUA still UNDER-reacts to its own signal and is now the only teacher whose beta exceeds 1 at three of four horizons. Level and responsiveness are separate defects; exactly one is fixed.
experiments.notes: NOT YET AN ADOPTION. eval/functional_barriers.py is the pre-registered gate and has not run: P2-scale-v2 improved QLIKE 9.7% and degraded every barrier metric, so a level change is never adopted here on QLIKE alone. That battery uses a PAIRED INTERVAL per barrier metric rather than the bare inequality that blocked P3-exogenous-barriers on 1e-5 movements (R69). CAVEAT CARRIED: the neural arm reproduces only to about 2e-3 unless the episode table is pinned byte-for-byte (P2-sample-sensitivity); the effects here are 0.005 to 0.096, one to two orders of magnitude larger, so the verdicts are safe and the decimals are not. NEXT: the barrier battery, then serving, then the slope. | READ OF THE SERVING PATH, added before the barrier battery returned, because it reframes what that battery can and cannot show. serve/predict.py line 104 already states the defect: 'QLIKE is minimised by the conditional MEAN of variance. sigma_med is a median. On the production slice the gap is a factor of 1.1250 and the published number was 12.5% low.' So the serving side measured the SAME gap independently -- 12.5% on the production slice at H=19 against 13.3% measured here at H=1 -- and fixed it with a FITTED TRAILING SCALAR (qlike_scale: a windowed empirical sqrt(mean(RV^2/sigma^2)) with a CLIP rail, lagged by the settlement requirement) when the model already computes the exact conditional mean in the same forward pass. THE ADOPTION IS THEREFORE NOT A NEW CORRECTION, IT IS REPLACING AN ESTIMATED CORRECTION WITH AN EXACT ONE: no window, no lag, no clip, no settled-episode requirement, and per-episode conditional rather than a trailing average. AND THE SAME COMMENT PREDICTS THE BATTERY'S RESULT: P2-scale-v2 put a level constant INSIDE the predictive object and lost all six barrier metrics, and P2-mean-level's SHUFFLED control lost them by the same amount, so 'the damage comes from moving the level at all, not from how the shift is obtained'. The battery feeds sigma_mean to the committee's quantiles(), which IS moving the level inside the predictive object. If it degrades the barriers, that is not a failure of this finding -- it is confirmation of the separation already shipped, and the correct adoption is then on the REPORTED scalar only, with sigma_med kept for the barrier curves. Both outcomes are therefore informative and neither threatens the QLIKE scorecard.

experiments.question: Can the REPORTED sigma scalar affect the barrier curves at all -- i.e. is the separation predict.py enforces by careful coding actually structural?
experiments.rule: Direct probe, not code reading. Build a Committee with all four specialists, feed it the SAME pred and two scalars differing by the measured median-to-mean factor 1.13, and compare the curves. Then change sigma_atoms by the same factor to prove the probe is not vacuous.
experiments.result:
THERE IS NO CHANNEL. THE SEPARATION IS STRUCTURAL.
  probe 1: a 13% change in the reported scalar sigma moves the barrier curve by max |dQ| = 0.000e+00.
  probe 2: a 13% change in pred['sigma_atoms'] moves it by 8.864e-03, so probe 1 is not vacuous.
  probe 3: removing sigma_atoms to force the fallback branch CRASHES in infer.safe_level, which requires it -- so the branch that reads the scalar is unreachable dead code in this pipeline.
MECHANISM, in the source: every specialist's quantiles() opens with `if sigma_atoms is not None: return _mix_over_sigma(z, sigma_atoms)` and Committee._stack always passes pred.get('sigma_atoms'). The NeuralSpecialist never takes a scalar at all -- it calls quantiles_from_pred. So the curves are a function of the model's DISTRIBUTION over sigma and of nothing else.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ADOPTION: publishing sigma_mean instead of sigma_med is safe BY CONSTRUCTION, not merely by test. P2-scale-v2's damage came from post_shift_fn, which rewrites the log-vol that FEEDS the quantiles -- a genuinely different operation from changing which scalar is printed. The two were conflated in predict.py's own comment ('the damage comes from moving the level at all'), and that sentence is true of the predictive object and false of the reported number.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE BATTERY: eval/functional_barriers.py reported every metric identical to 0.000 and 'DEGRADED: none'. That is not a pass, it is an absent channel, and reporting it as a pass would have been a guard that cannot fail (R2). The module now detects the all-zero case and records INAPPLICABLE instead.
CONSEQUENCE FOR AN EXISTING GATE: tests/test_level_report.py asserts the barriers are bit-identical when the reported scalar changes. By this finding that assertion cannot fail via this route. It still guards a future change that writes into pred, which is the thing that actually hurt P2-scale-v2, so it stays -- but its strength was overstated.
experiments.notes: Found by applying R65 to my own battery: an exact zero across all six metrics, with a paired Brier interval of exactly [0.00000, 0.00000], is a statement about the harness and not about the model. This is the fourth no-op of the session from the same error class -- measuring a quantity a pipeline cannot vary -- and the first one caught on the first run rather than after two or three wrong versions.

experiments.question: Ship it: does the served forecast report the conditional MEAN of variance, and does the change reach the reported number and nothing else?
experiments.rule: Adoption requires the serving gate, not an experiment. tests/test_level_report.py now runs forecast() twice against the same anchor -- once on each functional -- and requires exactly sigma_window_pct and sigma_annualized_pct to differ, the published number to BE the functional with nothing applied on top, and the gate itself to be shown capable of failing by leaking the change into the predictive object.
experiments.result:
ADOPTED. serve/predict.py publishes pred['sigma_mean'] and the fitted trailing scalar no longer multiplies anything.
LIVE ON THE CURRENT ANCHOR: sigma_med 2.067%, sigma_mean 2.640%, ratio 1.2774. The trailing scalar on the same anchor was 1.1113 -- so the EMPIRICAL ESTIMATE was under-correcting the median-to-mean gap by about a sixth, which is exactly the kind of error an estimate makes and an exact quantity does not.
WHAT WAS REPLACED: qlike_scale, a windowed empirical sqrt(mean(RV^2/sigma^2)) with a CLIP rail and a settled-episode lag, estimating the ratio between two functionals of a distribution the model already reports both of. Replacing it removes the window, the lag, the rail and the settlement requirement, and is conditional per episode where the scalar was a trailing average.
WHY NOT BOTH: a further fitted level correction on top of the exact conditional mean makes it WORSE at all four horizons (H=1 0.54119 -> 0.54815, H=6 0.33784 -> 0.34715, H=24 0.23768 -> 0.24825, H=168 0.18181 -> 0.18565). So the scalar is dropped rather than stacked.
SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: P3-barrier-channel proved the committee never reads the reported scalar -- the curves come from pred['sigma_atoms'] and a 13% change in the scalar moves them by 0.000e+00. This therefore cannot repeat P2-scale-v2, whose damage came from post_shift_fn rewriting the log-vol that feeds the quantiles.
GATE: 8/8, including that the published number equals the functional itself with nothing on top (mean run 2.64, median run 2.067), that the ratio the reported sigma moves by matches mean/median to 2e-4, and that the gate still detects a leak into the predictive object (18 barrier fields).
experiments.notes: THIS IS THE SECOND ADOPTION IN PHASE 2/3 AND THE FIRST SUBSTANTIVE ONE -- the first, P2-level-report-adopt, introduced the fitted scalar this one removes. The research side measures the change as 13.3% to 26.0% of raw pooled QLIKE, and as the difference between losing to the HAR family at all four horizons and beating every teacher in the zoo at three of them. TWO CAVEATS CARRIED: (1) the served number now moves by +27.7% on the current anchor, which is a large visible change for any reader of sigma_window_pct, and it is a correction of a 12.5%-to-27.7% under-statement rather than a new claim about volatility; (2) the research numbers come from the neural arm, reproducible only to ~2e-3 unless the episode table is pinned byte-for-byte, while these effects are 0.02-0.09. STILL OPEN: beta > 1. The functional fixes the LEVEL and leaves the responsiveness miscalibration untouched -- slightly worse, in fact -- and that is now the principal defect.

experiments.question: Can the adopted functional change be broken? An adversarial agent was given five attacks and returned 'probably wrong'.
experiments.rule: Its arguments are re-tested here, not accepted. The one testable attack is settled by measuring the calibration ratio mean(RV^2/sigma^2) on RAW output: a correct conditional mean of variance implies exactly 1.
experiments.result:
THE ADOPTION SURVIVES, AND ITS BEST ATTACK IS REFUTED IN THE DIRECTION OPPOSITE TO ITS PREDICTION.
CALIBRATION RATIO, raw output, no correction of any kind (1.0 is a perfect conditional mean under QLIKE):
  H=1    median 1.4318   MEAN 0.9630   har_short 2.0348
  H=6    median 1.4554   MEAN 0.9880   har_short 1.3929
  H=24   median 1.4434   MEAN 0.9915   har_short 1.2300
  H=168  median 1.1669   MEAN 0.8992   har_short 1.0493
The adopted functional is calibrated to within 1-4% at the three short horizons with NOTHING FITTED, where the median was off by 43-46%. This is the strongest available evidence that it is the right object: the fitted constant c that Phase 2 spent months on was closing a 44% gap that the model could close to 1% by itself.
ATTACK 2, QUADRATURE BIAS -- THE ONLY TESTABLE ONE, AND REFUTED. The agent argued that averaging 32 equally-spaced quantiles is a midpoint rule that under-estimates the mean of a heavy-tailed variable, so sigma_mean would be too SMALL and the ratio above 1. The mechanism is real but the sign is wrong: every measured ratio is BELOW 1 (0.963, 0.988, 0.992, 0.899), so the 32-atom average slightly OVER-estimates E[RV^2]. The residual is 1-4% at short horizons against a 44% defect, and 10% at H=168 which is worth noting.
ATTACK 5, 'NOT STANDARD PRACTICE' -- REFUTED BY EVIDENCE ALREADY IN HAND. arXiv 2607.05291, the 50-asset benchmark, states: 'The QLIKE-optimal forecast is the conditional mean of the variance... the conditional mean nonetheless remains preferable to the conditional median, which carries an additional bias.' The agent searched and reported finding no such statement.
ATTACK 4, 'DIFFERENT UNITS' -- CONFUSED. sigma_mean = sqrt(mean(variance)) is a volatility in the same units as the median it replaces.
ATTACK 1, 'THE ATOMS ESTIMATE A LATENT E[sigma^2], NOT E[RV^2]' -- WRONG. The atoms are quantiles of the predictive distribution of REALIZED vol, because that is what the pinball loss was trained against. The calibration ratio confirms it empirically: an estimator of the wrong quantity would not land within 1% of 1.
ATTACK 3, DOWNSTREAM HARM -- ASSERTED, NOT MEASURED, AND MOSTLY MISDIRECTED. Barrier curves and safe levels are what a position-sizer would read, and P3-barrier-channel proved they cannot see this change. The legitimate residue is the COMMUNICATION point, which was already recorded before the agent ran: the published number rises 27.7% and that is a correction of an understatement, not a new claim about volatility.
experiments.notes: WHAT THE AUDIT ACTUALLY BOUGHT: one number worth having. H=168's ratio of 0.8992 means the mean functional is about 10% too large at one week -- an order of magnitude larger residual than at the short horizons, and consistent with har_short tying it there. That is a real, narrow, previously unmeasured defect and it is the only thing from this audit that changes anything. Three for four on the session's agents: the headline was wrong and something smaller in the same report was worth keeping.

experiments.question: Is NOCTUA's under-reaction (MZ slope beta > 1) caused by AVERAGING THREE SEEDS, or is it intrinsic to the pinball loss and the signal?
experiments.rule: PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE THE RUN. Rebuild teacher_oof with --seeds 1 and compute beta for the mean functional at all four horizons, against the 3-seed values 1.303 / 1.236 / 1.116 / 0.915. Nothing else changes: same corpus, same architecture, same loss, same folds. BANDS: a single-seed beta LOWER by more than 0.05 at H=1 means averaging is compressing the forecast distribution and the remedy is the aggregation method; within 0.05 means averaging is exonerated and the defect is intrinsic to the loss or the signal; HIGHER means averaging is helping and a single model is worse. Run sequentially after the artifact regeneration, never alongside it -- three concurrent jobs of this kind were OOM-killed today (R75).
experiments.result: pre-registered before the run. PREDICTION, AND IT IS AGAINST MY OWN EARLIER SUSPICION: I proposed seed averaging as the likely cause, on the general ground that averaging forecasts compresses their dispersion. A literature search then found that parameter averaging (Vincentization) PRESERVES under-dispersion rather than creating it, and that pinball loss on a low-signal target is the better-documented mechanism. So I now predict beta(1 seed) is within 0.05 of beta(3 seeds) -- that is, my own suspicion refuted and averaging exonerated. Confidence MODERATE. Recording the reversal explicitly because predicting what I first suspected would be the easier thing to write down.
experiments.notes: WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT NEXT EXPERIMENT: beta > 1 is the only substantive defect left after the functional adoption, NOCTUA is the only teacher in the zoo that exhibits it, and the two candidate causes -- the aggregation and the loss -- imply completely different remedies. One cheap run discriminates them. If averaging is exonerated, the next step is a CRPS-trained variant, which the literature identifies as the distributional loss most likely to produce better-dispersed forecasts; no paper trains a volatility net directly on QLIKE, so that route has no precedent to borrow.

experiments.question: Can the ten-gate precommit suite detect a NameError in code that nothing reruns?
experiments.rule: Run `ruff check --select F821` over model/ and scripts/. Any hit is a live crash on that line. For each hit, establish the blast radius by asking which ARTIFACTS were written, after the introducing commit, by modules that reach the line -- a latent crash that nothing has rerun has corrupted nothing.
experiments.result: NO -- and not marginally. ruff F821 found TWO live NameErrors. (1) `direction.block_bootstrap_ci` referenced `block_len`, a parameter added on 2026-08-28 to the signature of `mean_ci` -- the function immediately below it -- and never to its own. Every call raised NameError, across 14 call sites in the eval suite, for 106 commits; verified live, `block_bootstrap_ci(normal(500))` raises. (2) `anchor_freshness._verdict` read the episode-level `spike` mask as a free variable off `main`'s scope. Both fixed: block_len threaded into the signature (default None reproduces pre-2026-08-28 behaviour exactly, so no published number moves), spike passed as a parameter with the --from-json path explicitly reporting the spike/calm split as UNAVAILABLE rather than silently omitting it. BLAST RADIUS: NIL. No artifact in model/artifacts was written after 2026-08-28 06:28 UTC by any of the 14 callers, so no published result on this branch passed through the broken function -- which is also precisely why it survived: the bug was latent, and latency is what hides from a test suite.
experiments.notes: WHY TEN PASSING GATES SAID NOTHING. Every one of the ten executes code, and neither defect is on a path anything executes: the first sits in modules nothing had rerun since August, the second behind an `all("_q" in r ...)` guard the stored-fold path does not satisfy, so the diagnostic silently did not exist rather than failing. A test suite's coverage is its reachable set; a static check's is the whole file. F821 is now the FIRST gate in scripts/precommit.sh and in model-ci.yml, and the two gates CI ran that precommit did not (pitfalls --self-test, teacher_ledger --validate) were added, so the script's claim to run 'the same ones CI runs' is now true rather than aspirational. Recorded as REJECT against the suite, not as a neutral finding: the question was whether the gates were sufficient and the answer is that they were not.

experiments.question: Is NOCTUA's MZ slope defect (beta > 1) an INFORMATION defect, or an affine miscalibration that a two-parameter map already removes out of sample?
experiments.rule: Take the mean functional. Fit MZq on each fold's CALIB slice, apply it to that fold's TEST slice, then RE-MEASURE the MZ slope on the test rows the correction never saw. Out-of-fold beta near 1 means the defect is affine and transfers; beta unchanged means the correction does not generalise and the defect is real.
experiments.result: IT SPLITS BY HORIZON, and that was not the expected answer. Out-of-fold beta after MZq: H=1 1.303 -> 1.006, H=6 1.236 -> 1.019, H=24 1.116 -> 1.047, H=168 0.915 -> 0.916. At H=1 and H=6 the correction is fitted on calib, applied to test, and the slope lands on 1 -- the under-reaction is a STABLE AFFINE miscalibration that transfers across the fold boundary, not missing information. At H=168 the correction does nothing at all (0.915 -> 0.916), and the per-fold slopes it fitted say why: [1.009, -0.017, 0.757, 0.467, 0.388, 0.761]. A NEGATIVE slope in the 2022 calib slice means that fold's calibration data asserted that the more NOCTUA forecasts, the less volatility realises. That is not a correction, it is noise being fitted, and a 6x spread across folds at one horizon is the signature of an estimator without enough independent observations -- at H=168 with hourly anchoring, consecutive episodes share 167 of their 168 hours, so 8,760 test rows carry on the order of 52 independent windows.
experiments.notes: THIS REDIRECTS THE NEXT STEP, AND AGAINST MY OWN WRITTEN PLAN. P3-seed-dispersion's notes name a CRPS-trained variant as the indicated remedy for beta > 1, on the ground that beta > 1 is 'the only substantive defect left'. At H=1 and H=6 there is now nothing for CRPS to fix that two out-of-sample parameters do not already fix, so aiming a retrain there would be tuning against a solved problem. The live problem is at H=168 and it is NOT a loss problem: it is that the correction cannot be estimated from ~52 independent windows per fold. Remedies for that are about the estimator (shrink beta toward 1, or estimate it on an expanding window of PAST folds only) and not about the network. Note also that 2022 -- Terra, 3AC, FTX -- is the outlier fold at every single horizon (1.006 / 0.864 / 0.598 / -0.017 against neighbours of ~1.4 / ~1.35 / ~1.2 / ~0.76), so one regime year drives much of the instability. CAVEAT ON SCOPE: serving reports the RAW mean with sigma_scale.applied false, so none of this is an argument that serving is already corrected; it is an argument about what the defect IS. Adopting MZq into the serving path would be a separate decision needing its own evidence, and the H=168 instability above is a reason to be careful about it rather than a reason to rush.

experiments.question: Is the H=168 failure of the MZ correction regime variation (2022 being Terra/3AC/FTX), or is the correction simply fitted on too few independent windows to estimate?
experiments.rule: Count the INDEPENDENT windows in the slice the correction is FITTED on -- calib, not test -- as n/H, since episodes are anchored hourly against an H-hour forward window. Then check whether out-of-fold transferability tracks that count. Separately, test the regime reading directly: if 2022 is a regime outlier its calib and test slopes should agree with each other and disagree with other folds; if it is noise, its calib slope should disagree with its OWN test slope.
experiments.result: REGIME IS REFUTED; IT IS SAMPLE SIZE. Calib independent windows per fold are 4,247 / 707 / 176 / 24 at H = 1 / 6 / 24 / 168, and out-of-fold transferability is AFFINE / AFFINE / PARTIAL / UNESTIMABLE in exactly that order. The ordering is monotone in the window count and in nothing else in the table. At H=168 a two-parameter regression is being fitted on TWENTY-FOUR effective observations per fold, and the slopes it returns say so: [1.009, -0.017, 0.757, 0.467, 0.388, 0.761]. The direct test kills the regime reading outright: 2022's calib slope at H=168 is -0.017 and its TEST slope at the same horizon is 0.918, which is entirely ordinary against its neighbours [0.844, 0.918, 0.573, 0.534, 0.789, 0.777]. An estimate that disagrees that violently with the slice next door is noise. I had written 2022 up as the outlier fold at every horizon and attributed it to the 2022 credit events; that attribution was wrong and is withdrawn.
experiments.notes: TWO CORRECTIONS TO PUBLISHED NUMBERS, BOTH UNFAVOURABLE TO NOCTUA. The pooled raw beta understates the per-fold defect at both ends: H=1 pooled 1.303 against median-fold 1.370, H=168 pooled 0.915 against median-fold 0.783. Pooling stacks six folds carrying six different levels and that mixture moves the slope, so the pooled beta is not a slope any single forecast has. The same mechanism refutes a comment beta_stability.py shipped with -- that the per-fold c-rescale column equals raw 'by arithmetic' -- contradicted by its own output (1.334 vs 1.303). One level rescale cannot move a slope; six different ones can. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE PLAN: the CRPS retrain named in P3-seed-dispersion's notes is now poorly targeted at every horizon. At H=1 and H=6 two out-of-sample parameters already take beta to 1.006 and 1.019, so a new loss would be fixing a solved problem; at H=168 the binding constraint is 24 calibration windows, which no loss function changes. Indicated remedies are estimator-side: shrink beta toward 1 with weight set by effective sample size, lengthen the calibration window at long horizons, or borrow strength from the horizons where beta IS estimable. SCOPE, UNCHANGED FROM P3-beta-is-affine: serving reports the raw mean with sigma_scale.applied false, so none of this says serving is corrected; and the H=168 instability is a reason for caution about adopting MZq into serving, not a reason to rush it.

experiments.question: Closing P3-regularisation, which was left OPEN with its artifact already on disk. Does explicit regularisation reproduce the +1.46% that a shuffled noise column achieved at H=1?
experiments.rule: Score each arm's pooled QLIKE improvement against the shuffled-column bar, with the paired per-episode moving-block bootstrap at block max(round(n^(1/3)), 2H) and Bonferroni over the 16-member family. An arm reproduces the accident only if it BOTH clears zero AND reaches the bar MEASURED ON THE SAME SAMPLE.
experiments.result: THE QUESTION IS VOID AT H=1, BECAUSE ITS PREMISE IS FALSE ON THIS SAMPLE. The +1.46% bar was measured on the DVOL-era subset and imported as a threshold for arms running on the full 476,359 -- the R66 error, committed one commit after R66 was written. Re-running the col-shuf diagnostic on the SAME full sample as the arms gives -0.363% at H=1: the shuffled column HURTS. There is no accident at H=1 to explain, so no regulariser can be blamed for failing to reproduce it. At H=6 the accident is real but a third the size claimed, +0.363% rather than +1.24%, and there input noise at 0.15 reaches it: +0.378%, CI [+6.33e-04, +2.56e-03], clearing the corrected interval. So where an effect genuinely exists, under-regularisation IS an adequate explanation of it. H=24 and H=168 have no same-sample bar measured and therefore yield no conclusion; against the imported bar the two noise arms at H=168 show +0.438% and +0.632% on the point estimate but neither clears zero, so nothing is established there either.
experiments.notes: MY PREDICTION WAS WRONG WHERE IT WAS SPECIFIC. I predicted 'weight decay helps more than input noise'. At H=6, the only arm reaching the bar is input NOISE at 0.15; weight decay at 1e-2 reached +0.022%, seventeen times short. The weight-decay gains are real in the sense that they clear zero at H=1 and H=6 -- and negligible in the sense that they are +0.001% to +0.022% of QLIKE. With ~49,000 episodes an interval can exclude zero around an effect far too small to matter, which is R21: significance is not relevance. I also predicted 'nothing helps at H=168'; the noise arms' point estimates there are the largest in the table and simply fail to resolve, so that prediction is unresolved rather than confirmed. RECORDED AS NULL, NOT REJECT: the family established nothing, and the reason is a bar that was wrong before any arm ran. WHAT SHOULD HAVE CAUGHT THIS: the col-shuf diagnostic already existed in ARMS for exactly this purpose and was run 14 minutes AFTER the arms, rather than before them. A diagnostic whose job is to validate a threshold has to run before the threshold is used. Queueing col-shuf at H=24 and H=168 would complete the picture; until then those two horizons stay unconcluded rather than being scored against a bar known to be wrong at the two horizons where it was checked.

experiments.question: MODEL_CARD 5.3 reports a spike RV/sigma ratio of 1.453 against 0.964 on calm nights, measured against sigma_med. Serving now reports sigma_mean and the published level rose 27.7%. What are both ratios under the adopted functional, on the production slice?
experiments.rule: PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE THE RUN. Production slice, H=19 anchored 17:00 UTC -- the same slice 7a measured, not a horizon chosen afterwards. Report the RV/sigma ratio on spike and calm episodes for BOTH functionals, using the same causal spike flag (levers.causal_spike_flag) and the same walk-forward folds. The ratios are DESCRIPTIVE, so no interval gates a verdict; what is registered is that both functionals are reported side by side and that the median column must reproduce 1.453/0.964 to within rounding, which is the check that the harness is measuring the same thing 7a measured. If it does not reproduce, the discrepancy is the result and the refresh is void until it is explained.
experiments.result: pre-registered before the run. PREDICTION: the spike ratio falls but by LESS than the full 27.7% level change, and the calm ratio falls by MORE, because a uniform multiplicative level change acts uniformly on a ratio only if the spike and calm slices share the same median/mean gap -- and the whole reason sigma_mean differs from sigma_med is the RIGHT TAIL of the predictive distribution, which is fatter on exactly the episodes the spike flag selects. So I expect the gap between the two ratios to NARROW rather than translate. Confidence LOW-MODERATE: this is a mechanism argument with no measurement behind it, and the production sigma is a BLEND of NOCTUA with Log-HAR under BLEND_W=0.25 plus a calibration, so the functional change reaches it diluted and the arithmetic of the raw zoo does not transfer.
experiments.notes: WHY THIS IS NOT JUST DIVIDING BY 1.2774. That would import a level factor measured on the live anchor onto a spike/calm decomposition nobody re-ran, and the spike/calm split is precisely where a level change need not act uniformly -- it is the R66 error in miniature. The card now carries the staleness as a caveat rather than a corrected number, and says which half of the finding still stands: the DIRECTION (spike nights under-forecast relative to calm) does not depend on the level at all, since both ratios move together under any uniform rescale; the MAGNITUDE does. NOTE ON A LEAD I CHECKED AND DROPPED: the card's pair (1.453 spike, 0.964 calm) is numerically almost identical to the teacher zoo's median-vs-mean calibration ratios (1.4318, 0.9630 at H=1), which looked like evidence that 5.3 was a functional artifact rather than a spike finding. It is not: the production sigma is blended with Log-HAR under BLEND_W and then calibrated, so it is a different quantity from the raw NOCTUA atoms the zoo scores, and the two are free to agree by coincidence. Recorded because the coincidence is striking enough that someone else will notice it and should not have to re-derive why it means nothing.

experiments.question: The stagnation supervisor flags phase2/level-scale as OSCILLATING: REJECT -> ADOPT -> REJECT across P2-armA-correction, P2-level-report-adopt and P2-mean-level-result. Does P3-functional-adopt make that a fourth flip, and does it contradict P2-mean-level-result, which tested the mean/median conversion and REJECTED it?
experiments.rule: Compare the two interventions by what they touch. P2's M1 applied the mean/median delta as a post_shift_fn, so the shift reached Stage B, the committee and every barrier curve. P3's adoption changes REPORT_FUNCTIONAL only, leaving sigma_atoms untouched. If the two are the same intervention, the barrier channel must respond to both; if they are different, P3's must be measurably zero where P2's was not.
experiments.result: NOT A CONTRADICTION, AND NOT A FOURTH FLIP. The two interventions differ in what they move, and the barrier channel measures the difference directly. P2's M1 shifted the level through the pipeline and the battery degraded across the board -- DSC 0.009104 -> 0.007169, about -20%, with MCB, Brier, CRPS, logs and pinball all worse -- and its ratio guard overshot from 1.2656 to 0.9120. P3's adoption moves the barrier curves by 0.000e+00, because the committee specialists build their curves from sigma_atoms and never read the reported scalar (P3-barrier-channel; sigma_atoms itself moves them 8.864e-03, so the channel is live and the zero is not an absent measurement). Same quantity, two different roles: P2 MOVED the level, P3 changed WHICH NUMBER IS REPORTED. THE OSCILLATION IS EXPLAINED, NOT MERELY SUPERSEDED. The decisive evidence was already inside P2-mean-level-result and was read as a rejection rather than as a diagnosis: M3, the SHUFFLED control, degraded every barrier metric identically to M1 (DSC 0.007254 vs 0.007169). A control that destroys the correction's content and reproduces the damage exactly proves the damage is a property of the INTERVENTION CLASS -- moving the level at all -- and not of the correction. Its own pre-registration had said so in advance: 'if the guards fail in the same pattern, then the barrier degradation is a property of moving the level AT ALL, and that closes the level question in the other direction'. It closed, and the closure was not acted on for eleven days.
experiments.notes: WHAT ALL THREE PHASE 2 DESIGNS SHARED. A trailing QLIKE scalar, a fitted per-fold constant, and the model's own per-episode delta are three different estimators of one number, and every one of them was aimed at MOVING THE LEVEL. The verdict oscillated because the designs disagreed about the estimator while agreeing about the intervention, and the intervention was the part that was wrong: there was no level error to fix. The served scalar was the median of a predictive distribution under a loss minimised by the mean, and the fix is to report the other functional -- which costs nothing, fits nothing, and moves nothing downstream. The supervisor's standing advice on an oscillation is 'a verdict that changes with the design is a property of the design'; the sharper version, earned here, is that when several designs oscillate on one question, the thing to question is what they all ASSUME rather than what they disagree about. ALSO WORTH RECORDING: P2-mean-level-result measured the model's own mean/median factor per fold as 1.2458/1.1362/1.2100/1.1769/1.1254/1.1227, scattering around the per-fold QLIKE optimum rather than sitting biased above it, which refutes the 1.205 constant the infer.py docstring recorded. That docstring has now been corrected.

experiments.question: A practitioner thesis: build a Fixed Range Volume Profile over a 24h window, and if price touches BOTH the value-area high and low during the following 22 hours, expect momentum -- do not sell, buy a straddle. Does the double-touch flag predict larger subsequent movement at the production anchor?
experiments.rule: DESIGN FIXED BEFORE THE RUN. In UTC the thesis is: FRVP over [D-2 19:00, D-1 19:00), observe [D-1 19:00, D 17:00), decide at D 17:00 -- which is exactly this project's production slice (H=19, anchor 17:00 UTC), so the flag is causal and available when the shipped model forecasts. Endpoints, all specified before any number was seen: (1) unconditional RV conditional on the flag; (2) INCREMENTAL over the Log-HAR anchor, because touching both edges requires the 22h range to exceed the value-area width and range is HAR's main input, so measuring against zero would measure volatility clustering; (3) the tail -- quantiles of |return| and of max excursion -- because 'momentum' is a tail event and a median test is the wrong instrument for it. EVERY arm paired with a WIDTH-MATCHED PLACEBO: an identical-width band centred on the window VWAP and on the window's high-low midpoint, places the profile did not choose. The placebo isolates the only thing FRVP adds over a range statistic, namely the POC's LOCATION.
experiments.result: NOT SUPPORTED, AND THE PLACEBO IS THE REASON. 3,293 production anchors, 2017-08 to 2026-08, double-touch rate 34.7%. (1) UNCONDITIONAL: median RV 0.02134 on double-touch days against 0.02183 otherwise, ratio 0.977 -- marginally the WRONG direction. (2) OVER HAR: in-sample coefficient on log RV is +0.0195, se 0.0137, t = +1.42, dR2 = +0.0002 against HAR's R2 of 0.6031. The VWAP-centred PLACEBO scores HIGHER on the same regression: +0.0268, t = +1.96, dR2 = +0.0005. A band of the same width centred where the profile did not point carries at least as much as the real one. (3) TAIL: P(|R| > t) lifts are 0.925 / 0.891 / 0.891 at the 80th, 90th and 95th percentile thresholds -- double-touch days are LESS likely to produce a large move. Only the 99th percentile lifts above one, at 1.076, where the placebo lifts 1.332. Max standardized excursion: ratio 1.004 at the median, 0.970 at p90. (4) The flag agrees with the VWAP placebo on 89.5% of days and with the midpoint placebo on 83.5%; the POC's location changes the flag on 158 of 1,142 double-touch days. (5) BY YEAR: 4 of 10 years run in the thesis direction, which is a coin flip, and there is no recent-regime rescue -- 2025 is 0.960 against, 2026 is 1.051 for.
experiments.notes: WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT TEST, because the thesis is a TRADE and this is a volatility measurement. NOT TESTED, and not testable here: the straddle's profitability, which depends on IMPLIED vol at entry against realized. A day with slightly lower realized vol is still a winning straddle purchase if implied is cheaper still, and this repository has no option prices, spreads or fills -- R28 forbids manufacturing that P&L and it is not manufactured. ALSO NOT TESTED: the primary selling rule (above POC sell VAH, below POC sell VAL). That one is NOT a direction forecast -- selling a strike is a bet it is not TOUCHED, a first-passage question the committee already emits curves for -- so it is scorable against existing machinery and is the more promising half to run next. HORIZON CAVEAT, THE LARGEST: movement is measured over H = 19h from 17:00 UTC, the production window. If the intended straddle expires on a different clock the test does not bind, and re-running at the true expiry horizon would be a fair objection to everything above. MY OWN EXPLANATION ALSO FAILED: I proposed that a two-sided sweep is a REJECTION of both edges and therefore a consolidation signature, which would make lower forward vol coherent rather than surprising. Days closing back inside the value area are 33.3% of double-touch days against 33.0% otherwise -- no difference, so that story is unsupported and is recorded as unsupported rather than quietly dropped. THE ONE SURVIVING THREAD: the 158 days the POC's location flags and the placebo does not show median RV 4.3% above days neither flags. That is a post-hoc subset chosen after seeing where the placebo agreed, n is small, and it would need its own pre-registered test before it means anything. PROVENANCE: supplied by the user as a 'proven thesis'. It is recorded as a hypothesis and tested adversarially, which is the standing instruction; a disagreement between this result and the user's own evidence most likely lives in the horizon or in the implied-vol leg, neither of which this run covers.

experiments.question: The other half of the FRVP thesis: at the production anchor, above POC sell VAH and below POC sell VAL. Scored as FIRST PASSAGE rather than as direction -- selling a strike is a bet it is not touched -- does the value-area edge place a strike better than a constant-percentage strike at the same distance?
experiments.rule: Family of 8 fixed before reading any interval: 4 horizons (6, 19, 24, 48h from the 17:00 UTC anchor) x 2 metrics. METRIC 1 is P(touched before expiry), which is what a seller who stops out cares about. METRIC 2 is ITM at expiry, which is what a seller who HOLDS loses on -- being touched is not being assigned, since price can trade through a strike and expire back inside. CONTROL, distance-matched: a constant-percentage strike at the median distance of the rule's strike over the EXECUTABLE days. Paired on identical days, moving-block bootstrap at block 2, Bonferroni over the family of 8 -> 99.375% intervals. Days where spot is ALREADY beyond the rule's strike at entry are excluded, since no one sells a strike already breached.
experiments.result: NOT ESTABLISHED, BUT NOT REFUTED, AND THE SIGNS ARE ALL ONE WAY. 0 of 8 rows clear the corrected interval. Every one of the 8 point estimates favours the rule, from +0.18pp to +3.31pp. Best rows: touch at H=24 +3.31pp [-0.37, +6.98] and H=19 +3.12pp [-0.69, +6.98], both of which clear an UNCORRECTED 95% interval and neither of which survives the correction the family demands. On the held-to-expiry metric the edge is much smaller -- +0.18pp at H=19, +2.20pp at H=24 -- so what edge exists is about the intraday PATH, not the expiry outcome, and would only be worth anything to a seller who manages on touch. THE BIGGER FINDING IS EXECUTABILITY: on 66.9% of days spot is already beyond the strike the rule names by the time the decision is made. Only 1,089 of 3,293 anchors are tradeable at all. The value area is built from a window that ended 22 hours earlier and its half-width is about 1% of price, which BTC covers easily in 22 hours -- so the level is usually stale by entry. The rule's strike sits a median 0.60% from spot on the days it IS executable, i.e. it is a near-ATM sale, which is why absolute touch rates are high (68.1% at H=19).
experiments.notes: A CONTROL BUG THAT REVERSED THE ANSWER, worth recording because it was mine and it was large. The distance-matched control first took its median distance over ALL rows, including days where spot was already beyond the strike -- whose 'distance' is a distance to something already breached and is not a strike anyone would sell. That inflated the control's distance and made the rule look 9 to 19 percentage points WORSE than the control. Computing the median over executable days only flips the sign to the rule's favour by 2 to 3 points. A control is an estimate and can be wrong in either direction; this one was wrong in the direction that would have killed the thesis. THE SECOND CONTROL IS NOT A CONTROL. The VWAP-centred band edge is touched less often (63.1% vs 68.1% at H=19) but sits FARTHER from spot (0.72% vs 0.60%), and touch probability falls with distance, so the comparison measures the distance and not the placement. It is reported but must not be read as evidence either way; only the distance-matched control bears on the question. ON THE CONSISTENT SIGNS: 8 of 8 in one direction looks like strong evidence and is not. The rows share days, the horizons are nested, and the two metrics are strongly correlated, so the effective number of independent tests is far below 8 and a sign count over them is close to meaningless (R21). What it does justify is a properly powered, pre-registered test at ONE horizon and ONE metric chosen in advance -- which is the next step if this is pursued. NOT TESTED: premium. A nearer strike earns more, so a touch-rate comparison at matched distance is not a P&L, and this repository has no option prices (R28).

experiments.question: Are P3-frvp-double-touch and P3-frvp-sell-rule artifacts of the free parameters? A thesis arrives with its parameters already chosen by whoever found it, so coverage and bin count are forking paths until swept.
experiments.rule: Sweep coverage in {0.60, 0.70, 0.80, 0.90} x bins in {32, 64, 128}, 12 settings, 2024-01 onward. Report the value-area half-width, the share of days spot is still INSIDE the area at decision (executability), the double-touch rate, and the width-matched placebo's rate at every setting. The double-touch REJECT stands only if the placebo matches or exceeds the real flag at EVERY setting, not merely at the default.
experiments.result: BOTH FINDINGS ARE PARAMETER-ROBUST; NEITHER IS AN ARTIFACT. (1) BIN COUNT DOES NOTHING. Across 32/64/128 the half-width moves by at most 0.01pp and executability by at most 1.6pp at fixed coverage. One forking path closed outright. (2) THE PLACEBO MATCHES OR EXCEEDS THE REAL FLAG AT EVERY ONE OF THE 12 SETTINGS: 39.6 vs 36.1 at coverage 0.60, 32.1 vs 30.2 at 0.70, 25.6 vs 25.0 at 0.80, 19.4 vs 18.2 at 0.90 (bins 32 shown; 64 and 128 the same to within a point). The double-touch REJECT does not depend on the default and cannot be tuned away. (3) EXECUTABILITY NEVER RECOVERS. Spot is inside the value area at decision on 25.6% of days at coverage 0.60, rising only to 42.7% at 0.90 -- still a minority. The half-width runs 0.64% to 1.23% of POC against a median 22h drift of 1.70%, so the level is stale on most days at every setting. (4) THE TWO HALVES OF THE THESIS PULL THE SAME PARAMETER IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS: widening coverage improves executability for the sell rule (25.6% -> 42.7%) and simultaneously starves the double-touch flag (36.1% -> 18.2%). There is no coverage that serves both.
experiments.notes: The 22h gap, not the coverage, is the binding constraint, and it is the one parameter that cannot be swept without becoming a different thesis -- the gap IS the rule as given. Shortening it would raise executability mechanically and is therefore not reported here as a proposal, because a parameter tuned until the result appears is not a test of the thesis that was handed over. If the user's own value areas are materially wider than 0.6-1.2% of price at half-width, then we are computing different objects and that discrepancy should be resolved before anything else in either entry is trusted. ALSO: `--sensitivity` is implemented as a flag on eval/frvp.py because the module's own docstring had promised it while an earlier version did not implement it -- the defect R34 names, committed in the same file that carries a corrected instance of it.

experiments.question: A second practitioner thesis: aggregate open interest across venues concentrates at strikes the market then does not break, with each venue rolling to its next expiry as its current one settles. Can it be tested here?
experiments.rule: Establish what data the test needs and whether it exists before designing anything. The test needs open interest BY STRIKE AND EXPIRY, historically, at daily or finer resolution.
experiments.result: NOT TESTABLE TODAY, AND NOT BACKFILLABLE. The repository contains no open-interest or options-chain data of any kind; the `strike` matches in the codebase are NOCTUA's own barrier levels, not an options chain. Deribit's `get_book_summary_by_currency` with kind=option carries per-instrument open_interest and volume and is the right source -- this repository already calls Deribit for funding and DVOL, and data/newdata/dvol_btc.parquet is the proof that the path works -- but that endpoint reports the chain AS IT STANDS NOW. Deribit publishes no public history of per-strike open interest, so the series cannot be reconstructed: a snapshot nobody took is gone. The thesis is therefore not refuted and not supported; it is unmeasurable until history is accumulated, which is why eval/harvest_oi.py and .github/workflows/harvest-oi.yml are added now rather than after some future decision to test it. Every day without a snapshot is a day that cannot be bought later.
experiments.notes: SCOPE AND HONESTY ABOUT THE BUILD. (1) The live fetch path is UNVERIFIED from the session that wrote it: this environment's egress policy returns 403 for deribit.com, which the proxy runbook says to report rather than retry, so only the parser is exercised locally (11/11 offline). The GitHub Actions runner does reach Deribit, and --live is what runs there; the first scheduled run is what will actually confirm the response shape. (2) DERIBIT ONLY, where the thesis says to pool venues. It is the venue this repository already reaches and the largest listed BTC options venue, so it is the right first cut, but the schema carries a `venue` column from day one so OKX, Bybit or CME can be appended rather than retrofitted. (3) THE EXPIRY ROLL NEEDS NO LOGIC: a full-chain snapshot carries every listed expiry each day and each instrument names its own, so the thesis's roll rule becomes a GROUP BY at analysis time rather than a stateful rule that can desynchronise. (4) NOTHING ACCUMULATES UNTIL MERGE -- scheduled workflows fire only from the default branch. (5) WHEN THERE IS HISTORY, THE TEST IS FIRST PASSAGE, NOT DIRECTION: 'the market does not break the max-OI strike' is a question about whether price REACHES a level, which the committee already emits curves for, so it is scorable without option prices (R28) and does not run into the closed direction result. A PARSER DEFECT CAUGHT BY ITS OWN FIXTURE BEING REBUILT: the first max-OI fixture picked a winner that won whether or not calls and puts were pooled, so it could not have detected a failure to pool, and its assertion named the wrong strike besides. Rebuilt so that pooling changes the answer (120000 wins at 250 only when summed, against 100000 at 200).

experiments.question: Closing P3-seed-dispersion. Is NOCTUA's under-reaction (MZ slope beta > 1) caused by AVERAGING THREE SEEDS, or is it intrinsic to the loss and the signal?
experiments.rule: As pre-registered: rebuild teacher_oof with --seeds 1, compute beta for the mean functional at all four horizons against the 3-seed values 1.303 / 1.236 / 1.116 / 0.915. Nothing else changes. BANDS, fixed in advance: a single-seed beta LOWER by more than 0.05 means averaging compresses the forecast distribution and the remedy is the aggregation; within 0.05 means averaging is exonerated and the defect is intrinsic to the loss or the signal; HIGHER means averaging is helping.
experiments.result: AVERAGING IS EXONERATED AT ALL FOUR HORIZONS, and the pre-registered prediction -- made AGAINST my own earlier suspicion -- is confirmed. Single-seed beta: 1.287 / 1.217 / 1.094 / 0.913 against the three-seed 1.303 / 1.236 / 1.116 / 0.915. Deltas -0.016 / -0.019 / -0.022 / -0.002, every one inside the +/-0.05 band and the largest of them less than half of it. HONEST DETAIL ON THE SIGN: all four deltas are NEGATIVE, which is the direction my original suspicion predicted -- a single seed is very slightly less under-reactive than the average of three, i.e. averaging does compress, faintly. But the magnitude is an order of magnitude below the band, so the mechanism is real and negligible. Reporting the consistent sign rather than only the band verdict, because 'within the band' and 'no effect at all' are different statements and the data supports the first.
experiments.notes: WHAT THIS SETTLES, TOGETHER WITH P3-beta-sample-size. The beta defect is not in the aggregation (this entry) and not an information defect at the short horizons, where a two-parameter correction fitted on calib takes beta to 1.006 and 1.019 on test rows it never saw. At H=168 the correction cannot be estimated at all from 24 independent calibration windows per fold. So every candidate remedy that acts on the NETWORK -- a different aggregation, a CRPS-trained variant -- is aimed at something that is either already removable out of sample or is a sample-size problem no loss function touches. The CRPS retrain named in the original entry's notes is formally withdrawn as the indicated next step. WHAT I GOT RIGHT AND WHY IT IS WORTH RECORDING: I first proposed seed averaging as the likely cause on the general ground that averaging forecasts compresses dispersion, then found that parameter averaging preserves under-dispersion rather than creating it, and pre-registered the REVERSAL -- predicting my own earlier hypothesis would be refuted. It was. Recording this because the alternative, predicting what I first suspected, would have been the easier thing to write down and would have made a confirmation out of a refutation.

experiments.question: P3-beta-sample-size claimed the H=168 cross-fold scatter in the MZ slope is 'noise, not a regime'. Does a moving-block bootstrap standard error on each fold's own calibration slice support that?
experiments.rule: For each horizon, compare the sd of the per-fold fitted slopes against the mean WITHIN-fold bootstrap standard error of a single slope, blocking at 2H. If the scatter is what one fold's own error predicts, it is noise; if it exceeds it, there is real variation between folds. Justify the 2H block first by measuring the autocorrelation of the MZ RESIDUAL, since block length moves a slope's standard error only when the residual is dependent, not merely when the regressor is.
experiments.result: MY 'NOISE, NOT A REGIME' CLAIM IS REFUTED AT EVERY HORIZON. sd across folds against mean within-fold SE: H=1 0.200 vs 0.029 (6.9x), H=6 0.205 vs 0.050 (4.1x), H=24 0.235 vs 0.085 (2.8x), H=168 0.361 vs 0.150 (2.4x). The scatter exceeds what a single fold's own estimation error predicts at all four, so the per-fold slopes differ for real reasons and not only because each is imprecisely estimated. THE 2H BLOCK IS DATA-JUSTIFIED, which had to be established before the SE meant anything: the MZ residual is strongly autocorrelated on the real table -- acf(1) = 0.403 / 0.900 / 0.972 / 0.995 at H = 1 / 6 / 24 / 168, with the first lag where |acf| < 0.1 at None / 12 / 24 / 168. At every horizon the decay lag is of order H or beyond, so blocking at 2H is warranted by the data rather than by the overlap argument alone.
experiments.notes: WHAT SURVIVES OF THE EARLIER ENTRY AND WHAT DOES NOT. SURVIVES: the monotone relationship between out-of-fold transferability and the independent calibration-window count (4,247 / 707 / 176 / 24 against AFFINE / AFFINE / PARTIAL / UNESTIMABLE); 2022's calibration slope of -0.017 at H=168 against its own test slope of 0.918, which remains a large within-fold inconsistency and still shows that individual H=168 estimates are badly imprecise -- the bootstrap SE of 0.150 there is itself large. DOES NOT SURVIVE: the sentence 'it is noise, not a regime', and the withdrawal of the 2022 regime attribution that rested on it. Both components are present. The scatter is part genuine cross-fold variation and part estimation error, and I collapsed it to the second because one vivid within-fold contradiction was easier to see than a variance decomposition I had not yet run. THE REMEDY CHANGES WITH IT. If beta genuinely varies across folds, then lengthening the calibration window does not by itself stabilise the correction -- more data from a fold whose true slope differs is not more data about the next fold's slope. The indicated direction becomes a slope that is allowed to move, or shrunk toward a pooled value by effective sample size, rather than simply estimated on a longer window. What does NOT change: none of this argues for a retrain, so the CRPS variant stays withdrawn as the indicated next step.

experiments.question: P3-regularisation-result left H=24 and H=168 unconcluded because the same-sample col-shuf bar had never been measured there. What are those bars, and does any regulariser reach them?
experiments.rule: Run the col-shuf diagnostic at H=24 and H=168 on the SAME full sample the arms used, and score the regularisation arms against the bar measured there rather than against the DVOL-era number imported into the module.
experiments.result: AT H=24 THE ACCIDENT IS REAL AND NO REGULARISER COMES NEAR IT. Same-sample col-shuf at H=24 is +0.91% with CI [+0.00034, +0.00540], clearing zero -- a permuted copy of an existing column genuinely improves pooled QLIKE there. Against it the regularisation arms are +0.012% (wd-1e-3), +0.004% (wd-1e-2), -0.091% (noise-05) and -0.166% (noise-15); the best is seventy-five times short of the bar and none clears zero. So at H=24 'under-regularisation' is decisively the WRONG explanation for what the shuffled column does, which is the pre-registered falsification branch. AT H=168 NOTHING IS ESTABLISHED: the same-sample bar is +0.78% but its CI [-0.00224, +0.00576] contains zero, so there is no accident there to explain and no arm can be scored against a bar that is not itself distinguishable from zero.
experiments.notes: This completes the entry that was left with two horizons open. The full picture across all four: H=1 the same-sample accident REVERSES sign (-0.363%, the shuffled column hurts) so the question is void there; H=6 the accident is real at +0.363% and input noise at 0.15 reaches it (+0.378%, clearing); H=24 the accident is real at +0.91% and nothing reaches it; H=168 the accident does not clear. One horizon of four supports under-regularisation as the explanation, one refutes it outright, one is void and one is unresolved -- which is a far less tidy answer than either the original hypothesis or its rejection, and is the answer. WHAT THE WHOLE EPISODE COST AND WHY: the bar was imported across samples before any arm ran (R66), and the diagnostic that would have caught it existed in the module and was run fourteen minutes too late (R77). Everything above is the price of running a validation after the thing it validates.

experiments.question: P3-functional-adopt switched the served scalar to sigma_mean on teacher-zoo evidence, where noctua_v1 is the RAW network. Serving BLENDS with Log-HAR at blend_w=0.25. Does the adoption's justification survive on the pipeline it was actually applied to?
experiments.rule: Score noctua(median) against noctua_mean on the production slice -- H=19, anchor 17:00 UTC, blended exactly as the serving runtime blends -- paired on identical episodes, moving-block bootstrap at the slice's block length, Bonferroni at the slice's family. Separately compare the calibration ratio the adoption claimed against the ratio measured on that slice. REVERT if the median is better with an interval excluding zero; LEAVE AS-IS if not separated; either way correct the justification if it does not hold.
experiments.result: THE DECISION STANDS; THE REASONING THAT PRODUCED IT DOES NOT. Paired contrast on the served pipeline: noctua(median) 0.25619 against noctua_mean 0.26039, delta -0.00420 (-1.64%) favouring the MEDIAN, CI [-0.03105, +0.01798] -- NOT SEPARATED, with 2 of 6 folds favouring the mean. There is therefore no evidence-backed reason to flip the served scalar, and flipping a level decision on a point estimate is exactly how phase2/level-scale oscillated three times (R80). BUT THE ADOPTION'S STATED JUSTIFICATION IS FALSE ON THIS PIPELINE. It claimed the mean is 'calibrated to within 1-4% with NOTHING FITTED', citing ratios of 0.963 / 0.988 / 0.992 / 0.899. Those are the RAW network's. On the blended slice the mean's ratio is 0.8181 -- 18% over-forecasting -- against the median's 1.1231, 12% under. The median is the CLOSER of the two to 1 on the pipeline that is actually served. The mechanism is arithmetic and it checks: a uniform log-shift cannot change the mean/median RATIO, but it changes the level that ratio multiplies. The raw network sits at 1.43, so a factor near 1.2 lands close to 1.0 -- the zoo result. The blend already pulls the level to 1.12, so the same factor overshoots to 0.82. The blend was doing most of the level correction the mean functional does, and applying both double-corrects.
experiments.notes: THIS IS R66 IN A FORM THE RULE DID NOT NAME: importing a number across PIPELINES rather than across samples. I wrote R66, spent a session applying it to other people's thresholds (P3-regularisation's imported bar, the model card's spike ratio), and missed it inside my own adoption -- which was made earlier in this same session. The tell was available and unread: the adoption comment in serve/predict.py cites 0.54119 at H=1, a teacher-zoo number, as justification for a change to a blended serving path. A citation that comes from a different pipeline than the code it justifies is the same defect as a threshold that comes from a different sample. WHAT CHANGES IN THE CODE: the justification comment in serve/predict.py is corrected to say which pipeline its numbers come from and that the served-pipeline contrast is not separated; REPORT_FUNCTIONAL is left at 'mean'. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE DECISION: a properly powered contrast on the served slice. n is 2,046 episodes over 6 folds here against 49,000 in the zoo, which is why a 1.6% difference cannot resolve; the slice is small because the production configuration is one episode per day. If that contrast is ever run at greater power and the median wins, the revert is indicated and this entry is what it supersedes.

experiments.question: Closing P3-spike-ratio-refresh. What are MODEL_CARD 5.3's spike and calm RV/sigma ratios under the adopted functional, on the production slice?
experiments.rule: As pre-registered: production slice, same causal spike flag, both functionals side by side. The MEDIAN column must reproduce the card's 1.453 spike / 0.964 calm to within rounding; if it does not, the discrepancy is the result and the refresh is VOID until explained.
experiments.result: VOID BY ITS OWN RULE, AND THE RULE EARNED ITS KEEP TWICE. First run reported mean(RV^2/sigma^2) and got 3.1428 spike against the card's 1.453 -- a 116% discrepancy that looked like data and was a STATISTIC: the card quotes a MEDIAN of RV/sigma, QLIKE is calibrated by the MEAN of its SQUARE. Reporting both, the median column gives 1.5352 spike / 0.8868 calm against the card's 1.453 / 0.964: 5.7% and 8.0% off. Closer by a factor of twenty, and still not 'within rounding', so the refresh is VOID as registered rather than quietly accepted at 6-8%. Candidate explanations, none yet tested: a different fold set or date range behind 7a's numbers, a different spike-flag threshold, or an intervening pipeline fix. NUMBERS FOR THE RECORD, carrying that caveat -- under the MEAN functional the ratios are 1.3200 spike / 0.7700 calm against the median's 1.5352 / 0.8868.
experiments.notes: MY PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION IS REFUTED, AND CLEANLY. I predicted the spike ratio would fall by LESS than the full level change and the calm ratio by MORE, because the mean/median gap comes from the RIGHT TAIL of the predictive distribution, which is fatter on exactly the episodes the spike flag selects -- so I expected the gap to narrow non-uniformly. Measured: spike falls 14.0% (1.5352 -> 1.3200) and calm falls 13.2% (0.8868 -> 0.7700). Spike falls slightly MORE than calm, the opposite of the prediction, and the spike/calm RATIO is essentially unchanged (1.731 -> 1.714). The functional change acts almost exactly uniformly, which is what a uniform log-shift must do and what I argued against. The mechanism I proposed is not present at a detectable size. WHAT THE CARD SHOULD SAY: the DIRECTION of 5.3 stands under either functional -- spike nights are under-forecast relative to calm, by a factor near 1.7 in both columns. The MAGNITUDE quoted is a median(RV/sigma) under sigma_med and the served scalar is now sigma_mean, under which the spike figure is 1.32 rather than 1.45. The card is updated to carry both columns and the unresolved reproduce gap rather than a single number.

experiments.question: The MZ slope is worth +2.77% / +2.38% / -1.35% / -19.55% against a level-only rescale at H = 1 / 6 / 24 / 168, tracking the 4,247 / 707 / 176 / 24 independent calibration windows available to fit it. Can ONE rule, with no horizon-specific tuning, match the better of {level-only, full-slope} at every horizon?
experiments.rule: PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE THE RUN. Five arms, all fitted on CALIB only and applied to TEST, with the level re-optimised in closed form at whatever slope the arm uses. (1) c: level only, beta=1. (2) mzq: the full fitted slope.
